Se state leggendo, io sono morto, e qual.easy: If you are reading this, I am dead, and someone has respected my last wishes. I am surprised, and I thank you. My father, Silas Pell, began this file. He was your family's notary for forty years. I kept it for another thirty. Inside are letters, police reports, newspaper cuttings, a will and a report by a handwriting expert. It is everything two honest notaries could gather about a man who, according to the records, was never born.
Se state leggendo, io sono morto, e qual.short: If you are reading this, I am dead. Two notaries kept this file, my father Silas and I: letters, reports, a will and an expert's study of a man who, on paper, was never born.

Leggete i documenti nell'ordine in cui l.easy: Read the documents in the order I have put them, and do not skip any. And forgive my writing in the last pages: for some years now I have written badly, and some mornings I can hardly recognise my own handwriting.
Leggete i documenti nell'ordine in cui l.short: Read the documents in order, skipping none. And forgive my handwriting in the last pages: some mornings I do not recognise it.

Alle dieci del mattino, nel cimitero del.easy: At ten in the morning, in the village cemetery, the dead man was buried. The heirs, the priest and the writer of this report were present. The carpenter had closed the coffin the evening before, and no one opened it again, because that was the dead man's wish. The sky was grey. About twenty people came, nearly all of them out of curiosity.
Alle dieci del mattino, nel cimitero del.short: At ten the deceased was buried, in a coffin closed the night before and never reopened, as he wished. Some twenty onlookers.

Si annota, per scrupolo, la presenza in.easy: For thoroughness, I note one thing. At the far end of the cemetery, near the gate, stood a man nobody knew. He was short, and wore a black coat too large for him. During the blessing he was laughing. When I went over to ask his name, the gate was open and he was gone.
Si annota, per scrupolo, la presenza in.short: At the back of the cemetery stood a short stranger in a black coat too large for him. During the blessing he laughed. Then he was gone.

Si parla di te. Al mercato le conversazi.easy: People are talking about you. At the market they stop talking when you pass, and start again more quietly as soon as you turn the corner. The washerwoman swears she saw a little man dressed in black come out of your alley at dawn. She says he was whistling your favourite tune.
Si parla di te. Al mercato le conversazi.short: People talk about you. The washerwoman swears a little man in black left your alley at dawn, whistling your tune.

Si parla di te, e adesso lo si scrive an.easy: People are talking about you, and now they are writing about it too. The Gazette's gossip page has a heading: *Who Goes Out at Night?* Under it is a rhyming riddle about an heir "of good family and bad habits". It does not say your name. It does not need to: every rhyme is on your surname.
Si parla di te, e adesso lo si scrive an.short: The Gazette prints a rhyming riddle: *Who Goes Out at Night?* It does not name you, but every rhyme is on your surname.

Si parla di te, e lo fanno i bambini. Pe.easy: People are talking about you, and the children too. In the street they skip rope and sing a new rhyme: *Umber, Umber, who is he? Papa's face is what you'll see.* When you pass they stop singing and look at you. Then they start again, louder.
Si parla di te, e lo fanno i bambini. Pe.short: The children sing: *Umber, Umber, who is he? Papa's face is what you'll see.* When you pass they stare, and sing louder.

Non smentisci niente. Anzi, a chi ti chi.easy: You do not say it is untrue. In fact, when someone asks, you answer with half a smile and let people think what they like. In the weeks after, suppliers deliver quickly, creditors wait, and the undertakers give you a discount.
Non smentisci niente. Anzi, a chi ti chi.short: You deny nothing: you smile and let them talk. Suppliers hurry, creditors wait, undertakers give you a discount.

Ne parli con il parroco, con il direttor.easy: You talk to the priest, to the bank manager, to the ladies who do charity work. You say the rumours are lies, and that your family is hurt by them. They listen very kindly. Perhaps someone believes you.
Ne parli con il parroco, con il direttor.short: You tell the priest, the banker and the charity ladies it is all slander. Perhaps someone believes you.

Ti stai lavando il viso quando lo specch.easy: You are washing your face when, for a moment, you see another face in the mirror. It is younger, smaller, and it smiles a smile you have never smiled. You look again, and it is you again. But that smile stays on you all morning, and you cannot get rid of it.
Ti stai lavando il viso quando lo specch.short: For a moment the mirror shows another face, with a smile that is not yours. It stays on you all morning.

Nella vetrina di un negozio, mentre aspe.easy: You are waiting for the carriage in front of a shop window. Your reflection turns a moment before you do. Only a moment, the time of a glance. Then it goes back to its place, polite and precise, and copies you in everything. Almost everything: it is not holding its hat.
Nella vetrina di un negozio, mentre aspe.short: In the window your reflection turns a moment before you. Then it copies you in everything. Almost: it is not holding its hat.

Nella fotografia di famiglia appena riti.easy: You collect the family photograph from the photographer. Everyone is looking at the camera. Everyone except you: in the photo you are looking to the side, towards the door, and smiling. The photographer swears he changed nothing. You swear you have never smiled like that.
Nella fotografia di famiglia appena riti.short: In the family photo everyone looks at the lens. You look at the door, smiling as you never have.

Rompi il vetro con il palmo della mano,.easy: You break the glass with the palm of your hand, without thinking. The pain does you good: it is yours, and nobody else's. You wrap your hand in a handkerchief. For a while, in the evenings, you avoid anything that shines.
Rompi il vetro con il palmo della mano,.short: You smash the mirror with your hand. The pain is yours alone. For a while you avoid reflections.

Guardi più a lungo. L'altra faccia non s.easy: You look for longer. The other face does not come back, but it leaves you something: a clear, complete idea. It is as if someone had whispered it in your ear while you were thinking of something else.
Guardi più a lungo. L'altra faccia non s.short: The other face does not return, but leaves you an idea, clear and whole, as if whispered.

Sul tuo Journal, sotto gli appunti di ie.easy: In your Journal, under last night's notes, there is a page you do not remember writing. It is a formula, and it is right: more beautiful than anything you have ever found. The ink is from your inkwell. But the writing slants backwards.
Sul tuo Journal, sotto gli appunti di ie.short: In your Journal is a formula you do not remember writing. It is right, and beautiful. The handwriting slants backwards.

Una lettera senza mittente, imbucata in.easy: A letter arrives with no sender, posted in town. Inside, on the estate's own paper, is the answer to the problem that has troubled you for months. It is written with a confidence you have never had. The postmark is from last night. Last night, as far as you remember, you were asleep.
Una lettera senza mittente, imbucata in.short: An unsigned letter, on estate paper, solves your problem. Postmarked last night. Last night you were asleep.

Ti svegli alla scrivania del laboratorio.easy: You wake at the laboratory desk, pen in hand and neck stiff. In front of you are three pages full of calculations: all correct, all new. The first lines are in your handwriting. The last ones, smaller and faster, slant backwards.
Ti svegli alla scrivania del laboratorio.short: You wake at the desk before three pages of correct sums. The last lines slant backwards.

La formula funziona, naturalmente. Funzi.easy: The formula works, of course. It works so well that for a whole day you feel like a genius, and for a whole night you are afraid to fall asleep.
La formula funziona, naturalmente. Funzi.short: The formula works. By day you feel a genius; by night you dare not sleep.

La bruci nella stufa del laboratorio, fo.easy: You burn the formula in the laboratory stove, one sheet at a time, and watch the paper turn black until nothing is left. What you find by yourself is less beautiful. But it is yours.
La bruci nella stufa del laboratorio, fo.short: You burn it, sheet by sheet. What you find yourself is less beautiful. But it is yours.

Arriva un invito su carta pesante: una c.easy: An invitation arrives on heavy paper: dinner with respectable people, with the bank manager and two ladies who do charity work. All evening nobody mentions Umber. When you leave, your host shakes your hand for longer than usual and gives you an envelope: "For your research. Science needs respectable people."
Arriva un invito su carta pesante: una c.short: At a respectable dinner no one mentions Umber. As you leave, your host hands you an envelope: "Science needs respectable people."

Il circolo cittadino, quello con le polt.easy: The town club, the one with leather armchairs and a portrait of the king, invites you to become a member. They welcome you with a toast and a speech about progress. Later, in the library, the chairman takes you aside. Some members would happily pay for your research, as long as the estate's name stays out of the newspapers.
Il circolo cittadino, quello con le polt.short: The club makes you a member. The chairman offers money for your research, if the estate stays out of the papers.

L'università della capitale ti invita a.easy: The university in the capital invites you to give a lecture. The hall is full: professors, students, journalists, and at the back some veiled ladies taking notes. At the end an old professor stands up and offers you a grant. Then he adds, with a smile, that of course nobody believes the stories about the salt.
L'università della capitale ti invita a.short: Your lecture at the university is packed. An old professor offers you a grant, adding that no one believes the salt stories.

Accetti, ringrazi e non dici una parola.easy: You accept, say thank you, and say not one word too many. The money is good, the company is good, and the silence is perfect. On the way home you notice you have been whistling the whole way. And you do not know the tune.
Accetti, ringrazi e non dici una parola.short: You accept and keep quiet. On the way home you whistle a tune you do not know.

Rifiuti, gentilmente, e racconti di Umbe.easy: You refuse, politely, and talk about Umber: the cheques, the nights, your family. A very long silence follows. Then someone claps, and others join in, a little unsure. You have told the truth in a place where people do not, and strangely, someone liked it.
Rifiuti, gentilmente, e racconti di Umbe.short: You refuse and speak of Umber. After a long silence, someone claps. The truth, strangely, went down well.

La boccetta viene dalla farmacia, come t.easy: The phial comes from the chemist, like all the others: white salt, very pure, with the new label. In the water the colour starts to change, but not as it should. It turns red and stops there, like a wound that will not close.
La boccetta viene dalla farmacia, come t.short: The new salt turns the water red, and stops there, like a wound that will not close.

Apri il cassetto del laboratorio: le boc.easy: You open the laboratory drawer: the phials are empty. At the bottom of the glass there is only the smell, bitter. You breathe it in for a long time before you put them back.
Apri il cassetto del laboratorio: le boc.short: The phials are empty. Only the bitter smell is left.

La cassetta di zinco è ancora sotto la t.easy: The zinc box is still under the loose board by the stove, where your parents found it. There are **{0}** phials left. In twenty-five years the salt has turned almost ivory, and smells faintly of bitter almond. But in the glass it still does what it should: red, violet, green. Whoever drank it before you died in their bed. More or less.
La cassetta di zinco è ancora sotto la t.short: **{0}** phials are left. The salt has turned ivory, but in the glass it still goes red, violet, green.

La polvere bianca cade nel bicchiere d'a.easy: The white powder falls into the glass of water, and the colour starts to change: first red, then dark violet, then green like a pond. Your hand shakes a little. One sip is enough.
La polvere bianca cade nel bicchiere d'a.short: In the glass: red, violet, green. Your hand shakes. One sip is enough.

Il sale nuovo funziona, ma nel verso sba.easy: The new salt works, but the wrong way round. The other one goes out as always, quick and cheerful. But in the morning, when you try to come back, part of you stays outside the door, and will not come in again.
Il sale nuovo funziona, ma nel verso sba.short: The new salt works backwards: in the morning part of you stays outside, and will not come back in.

Il dolore dura un minuto, come raccontav.easy: The pain lasts a minute, as the Journal said: the bones, the heart, the floor. Then you go out into the city of stone, in the other's small, fast body, and the city belongs to you. You run over wet roofs, look at yourself in closed shop windows, light a cigar at a gas lamp and blow the lamp out. You laugh, and the fog laughs with you.
Il dolore dura un minuto, come raccontav.short: A minute of pain, then you go out in the other's small, quick body. You run on the roofs and laugh, and the fog laughs too.

Al mattino ti svegli nel tuo letto, con.easy: In the morning you wake in your bed, your shoes black with soot. In your pocket is a cheque signed with your name, and a ticket for a theatre you have never been to.
Al mattino ti svegli nel tuo letto, con.short: Morning: sooty shoes, a cheque in your name and a ticket to an unknown theatre.

Il dolore dura un minuto: le ossa che st.easy: The pain lasts a minute: the bones creaking, the heart jumping, the floor coming closer. Then comes a new lightness: a small, fast body, with no regrets at all, going out through the servants' door.
Il dolore dura un minuto: le ossa che st.short: A minute of pain. Then a small, quick body, without regret, slips out by the servants' door.

Al mattino ti svegli nel tuo letto, con.easy: In the morning you wake in your bed, your shoes covered in mud. In your pocket is a cheque signed with your name, but the writing slants backwards.
Al mattino ti svegli nel tuo letto, con.short: Morning: muddy shoes and a cheque in your name, in a backward-slanting hand.

Rovesci il bicchiere nel lavandino e gua.easy: You pour the glass into the sink and watch the red go down the drain, slowly, as if it did not want to. No one will know what you chose. Perhaps not even the other one.
Rovesci il bicchiere nel lavandino e gua.short: You empty the glass into the sink. No one will know what you chose. Perhaps not even the other one.

Rimetti la boccetta nel cassetto e giri.easy: You put the phial back in the drawer and lock it twice. When you go back to the others your hands are still shaking. No one will know what you chose.
Rimetti la boccetta nel cassetto e giri.short: You put the phial back. No one will know what you chose.

Gli eredi si sono riuniti nella bibliote.easy: The heirs met in the estate library the day after the funeral, at five in the afternoon. The curtains were closed, as always in that house. The fire was out, and no one asked for it to be lit. I broke the seals in front of everyone and read the document, which the dead man had written by hand two years before.
Gli eredi si sono riuniti nella bibliote.short: The day after the funeral, in the library, curtains drawn and fire out, I read the will to the heirs.

La tenuta, con il laboratorio, gli strum.easy: The estate, with the laboratory, the instruments, the animals and the debts, goes to the children, in equal shares. The Journal goes to whoever can read it. So far, nothing strange.
La tenuta, con il laboratorio, gli strum.short: The estate goes to the children, the Journal to whoever can read it. Nothing strange.

Segue una clausola, che il sottoscritto.easy: Then there is a clause. I had to read it twice, because those present asked me to: *"Should I disappear without explanation, or die in circumstances my notary judges doubtful, all the rest of my property, the money in the bank, the shares and the key to the study on the alley, shall go to my friend Mr. Umber, who will know how to put it to good use."*
Segue una clausola, che il sottoscritto.short: Then the clause: *"Should I disappear, or die in doubtful circumstances, all the rest, with the key to the study on the alley, shall go to my friend Mr. Umber."*

Nessuno dei presenti conosce un Mr. Umbe.easy: None of those present knows any Mr. Umber. No one knew the dead man had a friend. And no one, to tell the truth, knew the estate had a study on the alley.
Nessuno dei presenti conosce un Mr. Umbe.short: No one knows Mr. Umber. No one knew of a study on the alley.

Il sottoscritto annota che il defunto è.easy: I note that the dead man died in his bed, of a fever, with the village doctor beside him. The circumstances are not doubtful. But I will give nothing to anyone until this Mr. Umber comes to my office, in person and by day.
Il sottoscritto annota che il defunto è.short: He died of a fever, in his bed. But Mr. Umber gets nothing until he comes to me, in person and by day.

Prima di congedarsi, il sottoscritto ha.easy: Before I left I gave each heir a page of the Journal, torn out and sealed, with their name written on it by the dead man. These pages were in the will too.
Prima di congedarsi, il sottoscritto ha.short: I gave each heir a sealed page of the Journal, with their name on it in the dead man's hand.

*Sale di Lomax, la prima partita, e ness.easy: *Lomax's salt, the first batch, and no other. Dissolved in a glass of well water: red, then violet, then green. Only one sip, on an empty stomach.*
*Sale di Lomax, la prima partita, e ness.short: *Lomax's salt, the first batch, and no other. One sip, on an empty stomach.*

*Ho provato con il sale di altre farmaci.easy: *I have tried salt from other chemists, and nothing happens. I have tried a second batch from Lomax, and nothing happens. There must have been something in that first batch that was not written in the order.*
*Ho provato con il sale di altre farmaci.short: *Other salts fail, even a second batch from Lomax. The first held something unwritten.*

*Non sono io che esco di notte. Lo giuro.easy: *It is not I who go out at night. I swear it on everything I love. And yet in the morning I have his keys in my pocket, and he has mine. I have his shoes on my feet, and they are my size.*
*Non sono io che esco di notte. Lo giuro.short: *It is not I who go out at night. Yet in the morning I have his keys, and his shoes are my size.*

A metà della riga successiva la scrittur.easy: Halfway through the next line the writing changes: it gets smaller, faster, and slants backwards, as if the hand were pulling the other way. *Stop writing about me.*
A metà della riga successiva la scrittur.short: Then the writing changes, slanting backwards: *Stop writing about me.*

Una pagina di conti, fitta di cifre. A m.easy: It is a page of accounts, full of numbers. Halfway down there is a line underlined twice: *Lomax, chemist, by the bridge: six phials, paid in cash.* With that sum you could buy the whole shop.
Una pagina di conti, fitta di cifre. A m.short: Accounts. Underlined: *Lomax, chemist: six phials, paid in cash.* A huge sum.

Sotto, a matita, più piccolo, come scrit.easy: Below, in pencil, smaller, as if written in a hurry: *S. P. knows. S. P. has the key to the cupboard. Tell him nothing, not yet.*
Sotto, a matita, più piccolo, come scrit.short: In pencil: *S. P. knows. S. P. has the key to the cupboard. Tell him nothing.*

Il disegno accurato di una porta di legn.easy: It is an exact drawing of a wooden door with no handle and no lock, with the measurements of the hinges and an address: the alley behind the estate. Below is a single line: *It opens only from the inside. Remember that, when I am on the other side.*
Il disegno accurato di una porta di legn.short: A drawing of a handleless door in the alley behind the estate: *It opens only from the inside. Remember that, when I am on the other side.*

Sul retro, macchiata di fango, c'è l'imp.easy: On the back, dirty with mud, is the print of a shoe. It is small, too small for a grown man.
Sul retro, macchiata di fango, c'è l'imp.short: On the back, the muddy print of a shoe too small for a man.

Pieghi la pagina in quattro e la infili.easy: You fold the page in four and put it among your papers. After all, it is yours: your name is on it, written by your father. You will tell the others what you want, when you want.
Pieghi la pagina in quattro e la infili.short: You fold it and keep it. It is yours: your name is on it.

La mattina dopo, a colazione, leggi la p.easy: The next morning, at breakfast, you read the page aloud, word for word, skipping nothing. The others listen in silence. Someone looks at you gratefully. Someone else suspiciously: why are you being so generous?
La mattina dopo, a colazione, leggi la p.short: At breakfast you read it aloud. One looks grateful. Another, suspicious.

A colazione si parla poco. Chi ha letto.easy: Little is said at breakfast. Whoever read their page aloud did it quickly, between the coffee and the bread. The others put theirs in their pockets, and watch everyone else's pockets. Pell the notary left at dawn without saying goodbye, and his carriage left two deep tracks in the mud of the drive.
A colazione si parla poco. Chi ha letto.short: Little is said at breakfast, and everyone eyes the others' pockets. The notary left at dawn without a word.

Dalle finestre della sala da pranzo si v.easy: From the dining-room windows you can see the village of {0}: timber-framed houses crowded round the square, the market, the bridge over the river. On the hill, where there were sheep last year, Lady Carew's workmen have started digging for a big brick building. It will be an asylum, they say, the most modern in the county. Lady Carew has already said there will be few places, and only for respectable families.
Dalle finestre della sala da pranzo si v.short: From the window you see {0}. On the hill Lady Carew is building a modern asylum, with few places, for respectable families.

Resta da decidere che cosa fare del labo.easy: You must decide what to do with your father's laboratory. It is a long, low room at the back of the house, with windows black from smoke, alembics still dirty and a smell of acid that no breeze can carry away.
Resta da decidere che cosa fare del labo.short: There is still your father's laboratory: blackened windows, dirty alembics, a smell of acid.

Chiudete la porta a doppia mandata e app.easy: You lock the door twice and hang the key in the kitchen, where everyone can see it. The village finds out, as it always does, and is pleased: a family that locks up its father's laboratory is a family that wants a quiet life.
Chiudete la porta a doppia mandata e app.short: You lock the laboratory. The village approves.

Spalancate le finestre, lavate gli alamb.easy: You open the windows, wash the alembics, light the burners again. In the drawers you find lots of chemicals, well kept and labelled. Your father bought in large amounts: there is enough for years.
Spalancate le finestre, lavate gli alamb.short: You reopen the laboratory. The drawers hold chemicals for years.

Un rigattiere della città viene con un c.easy: A dealer comes from town with a cart and takes away the brass microscope, the precision scales and two crates of glassware. He pays well, and in cash. The cart goes right through the village, and everyone sees the old man's instruments bouncing under the cover.
Un rigattiere della città viene con un c.short: A dealer buys the instruments and pays well. The whole village sees the cart go by.

Al mercato si parla solo del funerale, e.easy: At the market people talk only about the funeral, and about the man in the black coat who was laughing at the back of the cemetery. The baker swears he was the devil. The sexton says he was someone the dead man owed money to.
Al mercato si parla solo del funerale, e.short: The market talks of the man in black who laughed at the funeral. The devil, says the baker; a creditor, says the sexton.

Nell'ufficio dell'impresa, tra rotoli di.easy: In the firm's office, among rolls of drawings and sample bricks, sits Lady Carew herself. She is a tall, straight-backed lady dressed in grey, with a leather-bound notebook always open on her knees. She listens to the foreman without looking at him, and takes notes.
Nell'ufficio dell'impresa, tra rotoli di.short: In the office sits Lady Carew: tall, in grey, a leather notebook on her knees. She listens and takes notes.

Quando ti vede entrare chiude il librett.easy: When she sees you come in she closes the notebook, smiles and asks if you have come to see "the future of charity in this county". The asylum will have a hundred beds, she says, but she does not yet know how to pay for the roof. Respectable families usually help. The others usually end up inside.
Quando ti vede entrare chiude il librett.short: Lady Carew asks for money for the asylum roof. Respectable families help, she says. The others end up inside.

Lady Carew ringrazia, scrive il tuo nome.easy: Lady Carew thanks you, writes your name in the notebook in small, neat writing, and promises you a brass plaque at the entrance. She walks you to the door arm in arm, as one does with relatives. Or with patients.
Lady Carew ringrazia, scrive il tuo nome.short: Lady Carew writes your name down and promises a plaque. She walks you out arm in arm, like a relative. Or a patient.

Il capomastro srotola i disegni sul tavo.easy: The foreman spreads the drawings on the table. A hundred beds, it is true, and hot water on every floor. But under the gentlemen's ward there is a floor you cannot see from outside, with windowless cells and doors that lock only from the outside. Next to it, in Lady Carew's small writing, it says: *interesting cases*.
Il capomastro srotola i disegni sul tavo.short: The plans show a hidden floor with windowless cells. Beside it Lady Carew has written: *interesting cases*.

Lo dici abbastanza forte perché lo senta.easy: You say it loud enough for the foreman, the errand boy and the woman washing the stairs to hear. By evening the remark will have gone round every tavern in the village, and many will think it brave. Lady Carew does not. She opens her notebook again and writes something, still smiling.
Lo dici abbastanza forte perché lo senta.short: You say it loudly. The village thinks it brave. Lady Carew does not: she smiles, and writes it down.

Sulla tomba del padre ci sono fiori fres.easy: There are fresh flowers on your father's grave. Not the ones from the funeral, which are dry now, but new flowers every morning: wild violets tied with string. The keeper says he has never seen who brings them. In the soft earth in front of the headstone are prints of small, quick shoes, which go three times round the grave and then leave.
Sulla tomba del padre ci sono fiori fres.short: Every morning there are fresh violets on your father's grave. In the earth, small footprints circle the grave three times.

Aspetti dietro un cipresso fino alle tre.easy: You wait behind a cypress until three, cold to the bone. Then the gate creaks, and a little man in a black coat comes in whistling, with a bunch of violets in his hand. He kneels in front of the headstone and talks to it for a long time, quietly, the way you talk to a mirror. You cannot understand the words. At the end you understand the laugh.
Aspetti dietro un cipresso fino alle tre.short: At three a little man in black comes in with violets. He talks to the headstone for a long time, as to a mirror. Then he laughs.

Quando esci dal nascondiglio il cimitero.easy: When you come out of your hiding place the cemetery is empty, and the violets are where they were.
Quando esci dal nascondiglio il cimitero.short: You come out: the cemetery is empty, the violets in place.

Raccogli le violette e le butti nel fium.easy: You take the violets and throw them into the river from the bridge, a handful at a time, as you do with things that bring bad luck. Among the flowers is a folded note: *For the old man, who sleeps so soundly.* The writing slants backwards.
Raccogli le violette e le butti nel fium.short: You throw the violets in the river. Among them, a backward-slanting note: *For the old man, who sleeps so soundly.*

La sede del sindacato dei muratori è una.easy: The bricklayers' union meets in a room above the tavern stable: a stove, a table and thirty men who have not been paid for six weeks. Lady Carew, they say, pays when the work is finished, but the work never finishes, because she changes her mind every Monday. Last night someone left an envelope on the table with six weeks' pay for everyone, in cheques. The men do not know if they can cash them.
La sede del sindacato dei muratori è una.short: The asylum bricklayers have not been paid for six weeks. Last night someone left their wages, in cheques. Can they cash them?

Gli assegni sono buoni, naturalmente. Gl.easy: The cheques are good, of course. The men all cash them on the same day, and the village bank has no money left until evening. For a month, in the tavern, they drink to the health of Mr. Umber, the bricklayers' friend.
Gli assegni sono buoni, naturalmente. Gl.short: The cheques are good. For a month the tavern drinks to Mr. Umber.

Gli uomini bruciano la busta nella stufa.easy: The men burn the envelope in the stove, and you pay for bread and soup for a week. When she finds out, Lady Carew sends you an ice-cold note: charity, she writes, must be done properly.
Gli uomini bruciano la busta nella stufa.short: They burn the envelope, and you pay for bread. Lady Carew sends you an icy note.

Lady Carew apre la busta davanti a te, g.easy: Lady Carew opens the envelope in front of you, looks at the cheques one by one and puts them in her leather notebook, without a flicker on her face. "Thank you," she says. "You did the right thing. I shall pay the workmen next week." And she really does. With Umber's cheques.
Lady Carew apre la busta davanti a te, g.short: Lady Carew takes the envelope and thanks you. The next week she pays the workmen. With Umber's cheques.

Nel Park, vicino allo stagno, un bambino.easy: In the Park, by the pond, a little boy is playing alone with a paper boat. The boat is a carefully folded cheque: you can still see the amount, the signature and the writing that slants backwards. A tiny gentleman in a black coat gave it to him, he says, "because I was sad".
Nel Park, vicino allo stagno, un bambino.short: A boy plays with a paper boat made from a cheque. A tiny gentleman in black gave it to him, "because I was sad".

Il bambino accetta la moneta con la seri.easy: The boy takes the coin, as serious as a banker, and gives you the wet boat. At home you open it on the table: the cheque is signed with the name of one of you. You burn it before it dries.
Il bambino accetta la moneta con la seri.short: You buy the boat. The cheque bears one of your names. You burn it.

Il bambino ci pensa a lungo, con la fron.easy: The boy thinks for a long time, frowning. "He said he was the grandfather," he answers at last. "Everybody's grandfather. He had lots of grandchildren, and I wasn't one of them, but he liked me anyway." Then he goes back to his game, and says nothing more.
Il bambino ci pensa a lungo, con la fron.short: "He said he was everybody's grandfather," says the boy. "And that he liked me anyway."

La madre è una lavandaia, con le mani ro.easy: The boy's mother is a washerwoman, with red hands and a tired voice. When you tell her about the cheque she goes pale, then thanks you, then asks whether your family needs someone to do the washing. You do, you find out: the house is big, and nobody wants to work at the estate.
La madre è una lavandaia, con le mani ro.short: You take him to his mother, a washerwoman. She thanks you, and offers to do the estate's washing, where nobody will work.

All'alba, nel Park, vicino allo stagno,.easy: At dawn, in the Park, by the pond, a young officer on leave is waiting for you. He is pale with anger, with two seconds and a case of pistols. Last night, at the tavern, a little man in black with his collar up spilled wine on him, insulted his sister and gave him a visiting card. On the card was your family's name. The officer wants a duel.
All'alba, nel Park, vicino allo stagno,.short: An officer challenges you to a duel: a little man in black insulted him and left a card bearing your family's name.

Venti passi, nella nebbia. L'ufficiale s.easy: Twenty paces, in the fog. The officer fires first and misses by a long way: his hands are shaking. You fire into the air. The seconds shake hands, and the officer hugs you and cries a little. For a year the village tells the story, and every time it gets better.
Venti passi, nella nebbia. L'ufficiale s.short: The officer fires and misses. You fire into the air. The village talks of it for a year.

Chiedi scusa per una cosa che non hai fa.easy: You apologise for something you did not do, with all the dignity you can find, and you pay for the wine. The officer accepts, stiffly. The seconds look disappointed. On the way home you notice that now it is your hands that are shaking.
Chiedi scusa per una cosa che non hai fa.short: You apologise for something you did not do, and pay for the wine. On the way home, your hands shake.

L'ufficiale guarda il biglietto, poi la.easy: The officer looks at the card, then at your signature, then at the card again. The writing on the card slants backwards; yours does not. For a moment he seems disappointed he cannot shoot you. Then he shakes your hand, and that same evening takes the card to Inspector Haskett, with your compliments.
L'ufficiale guarda il biglietto, poi la.short: The card's writing slants backwards; yours does not. The officer shakes your hand and takes the card to the Inspector.

Il parroco è un uomo grasso e gentile, c.easy: The parish priest is a fat, kind man with tobacco-stained fingers and a very good memory for funerals. He remembers your father's well: the low sky, the few people, the man laughing at the back. Above all he remembers the bearers, who had to stop halfway up the church to get their breath back. "It was as heavy as a stone," he says. "I told the notary. He said grief is heavy."
Il parroco è un uomo grasso e gentile, c.short: The priest remembers the funeral: the bearers had to stop. "It weighed like a stone. The notary told me grief is heavy."

Il parroco accetta, e la domenica dopo c.easy: The priest agrees, and the next Sunday he says a long, well-sung Mass. During the most solemn moment, at the back of the church, someone laughs softly. When you turn round, there is only an old woman asleep.
Il parroco accetta, e la domenica dopo c.short: During Mass, someone laughs at the back. You turn: only an old woman asleep.

Il parroco sfoglia il registro dei morti.easy: The priest leafs through the register of the dead. "The carpenter nailed the coffin shut the evening before, in front of Pell the notary and the village doctor. No one else. The notary wanted no one to open it again: it was the dead man's wish." He closes the register. "At the time it seemed an act of love. Now I don't know."
Il parroco sfoglia il registro dei morti.short: "They closed it the night before, with Pell the notary and the doctor there. The notary wanted no one to reopen it." Now the priest does not know what to think.

Ringrazi e te ne vai. Sul sagrato ti acc.easy: You thank him and leave. On the church steps you notice the priest watching you from the door and crossing himself. Perhaps for you. Perhaps for your father.
Ringrazi e te ne vai. Sul sagrato ti acc.short: As you leave, you see the priest cross himself. For you, or for your father.

In chiesa si sposa la figlia del sindaco.easy: The mayor's daughter is getting married, and all the important people of the village are in the pews, the family from the estate too. Halfway through, the priest asks if anyone knows a reason why these two should not marry. At the back of the church someone laughs. Everyone turns round. There is no one there, but on the last pew is a wedding present wrapped in black, with a card: *From Mr. Umber, with every good wish.*
In chiesa si sposa la figlia del sindaco.short: At the mayor's daughter's wedding someone laughs at the back. On the last pew is a gift wrapped in black: *From Mr. Umber.*

Lo porti fuori sotto la giacca, mentre i.easy: You take it out under your jacket while the priest carries on with the ceremony. In the cemetery, hidden behind a tomb, you open it. Inside is a set of beautiful silver cutlery, with your family's initials. Only the knives are missing.
Lo porti fuori sotto la giacca, mentre i.short: Outside you open it: silver cutlery with your family's initials. Only the knives are missing.

Gli sposi lo aprono al rinfresco, davant.easy: The couple open it at the party, in front of everyone. Inside is a set of beautiful silver cutlery, with your family's initials. The bride thanks the family from the estate for the wonderful present. But the mayor looks at the initials, and then looks at **{0}**, for a long time.
Gli sposi lo aprono al rinfresco, davant.short: The couple find silver cutlery with your family's initials. The mayor stares at **{0}** for a long time.

Il sindaco ha deciso che è ora di finirl.easy: The mayor has decided the sightings must stop. He wants a night watch: six men with lanterns and sticks, in the streets from dusk to dawn. But he has no men and no money. When he sees you come into the town hall he greets you with a big smile, the way one greets someone who can pay.
Il sindaco ha deciso che è ora di finirl.short: The mayor wants a night watch, but lacks men and money. He greets you with a big smile.

La ronda gira per un mese intero, con le.easy: The watch walks the streets for a whole month, with lanterns and sticks. It catches no one. But the village sleeps better, and knows who paid for the lanterns.
La ronda gira per un mese intero, con le.short: The watch catches no one, but the village sleeps better. And knows who paid.

Giri per le strade con altri cinque, una.easy: You walk the streets with five others, a lantern and a stick you do not know how to use. At three in the morning, at the end of the alley behind the estate, you see a small shadow stop, turn and raise its hat to you. The others did not see it. You do not tell them.
Giri per le strade con altri cinque, una.short: At three, in the alley behind the estate, a small shadow raises its hat to you. Only you saw it.

Il sindaco smette di sorridere. Una fami.easy: The mayor stops smiling. Later, at the tavern, he says that a family that does not want a night watch is a family that has something to do at night. Everyone at the tavern agrees.
Il sindaco smette di sorridere. Una fami.short: The mayor stops smiling. At the tavern he says whoever refuses a watch has business at night.

La chiromante di adesso è la figlia di q.easy: The fortune teller now is the daughter of the old one: the same red scarf, the same pale, almost white eyes, and a bigger tent, with an iron stove and her mother's portrait hanging on the pole. She takes your left hand, then your right, and smiles. "My mother told me about your family," she says. "She told me to get paid first."
La chiromante di adesso è la figlia di q.short: The fortune teller is the old one's daughter. She smiles: "My mother told me to get paid first."

La chiromante è una vecchia con un fazzo.easy: The fortune teller is an old woman with a red scarf on her head and pale, almost white eyes. She takes your left hand, then your right, then your left again, and frowns.
La chiromante è una vecchia con un fazzo.short: An old woman with almost white eyes looks at your hands, and frowns.

\"Due linee della vita\", dice. \"Una co.easy: "Two life lines," she says. "One short and one long. I don't know which one is yours." She closes your fingers over your palm, as if to keep something inside, and will not say anything else.
\"Due linee della vita\", dice. \"Una co.short: "Two life lines. I don't know which is yours." She says no more.

\"Vedo denaro\", dice. \"Molto denaro, e.easy: "I see money," she says. "A lot of money, and not yours. Signed by someone else." She laughs, with all the teeth she is missing. "Take it while it's there." On the way home you find a wallet in the mud, with no name in it.
\"Vedo denaro\", dice. \"Molto denaro, e.short: "I see money, signed by someone else." On the way home you find a wallet in the mud.

\"Vedo una porta\", dice. \"Tu stai da q.easy: "I see a door," she says. "You are on this side. Stay on this side." For once it seems very good advice, and that night you sleep as you have not slept for months.
\"Vedo una porta\", dice. \"Tu stai da q.short: "I see a door. Stay on this side." That night you sleep well.

La vecchia ti lascia andare la mano di c.easy: The old woman drops your hand suddenly, as if it were burning, and puts the coin back in your pocket. "This hand isn't yours," she says. "You borrowed it. Give it back." Then she closes the tent, and does not open it again.
La vecchia ti lascia andare la mano di c.short: The old woman drops your hand: "This hand isn't yours. Give it back."

Oggi, nel laboratorio, il pavimento ha c.easy: Today, in the laboratory, the floor moved under my foot: a loose board by the stove, put back with too much care. Under it was a zinc box, and inside six phials of dark glass, sealed with wax. Inside is white salt, as fine as sugar, a little yellow when you hold it up to the light. The label says: *Lomax's Pharmacy – first batch*. Tied to the box with string is a note in our father's writing: *A single sip. Then the door.*
Oggi, nel laboratorio, il pavimento ha c.short: Under a laboratory floorboard were six phials of white salt: *Lomax's Pharmacy – first batch*. And a note from our father: *A single sip. Then the door.*

Non abbiamo ancora deciso che cosa farne.easy: We have not yet decided what to do with them. Meanwhile, in the village, the baker came to cash a cheque signed by our father. It is dated last week: more than a year after the funeral. A little man in a black coat too big for him gave it to him, and bought all the bread in the shop and threw it in the river, one loaf at a time, laughing.
Non abbiamo ancora deciso che cosa farne.short: The baker has a cheque signed by our father and dated last week. A little man in black gave it to him and threw all the bread in the river.

Abbiamo pagato il fornaio, e ci siamo fa.easy: We paid the baker and got the cheque from him. The signature is our father's, there is no doubt. But it slants backwards, as if he had written it with the wrong hand.
Abbiamo pagato il fornaio, e ci siamo fa.short: The signature is our father's. But it slants backwards.

L'assegno brucia in fretta, con una fiam.easy: The cheque burns quickly, with a greenish flame, and nobody says anything. The baker, paid twice, has promised to keep quiet. And he keeps his promise for almost a week.
L'assegno brucia in fretta, con una fiam.short: The cheque burns with a green flame. The baker promises silence, for almost a week.

La polizia del villaggio è una donna sol.easy: The village police is just one woman: Inspector Nell Haskett, tall and thin, with a black notebook and a pencil always sharp. She holds the cheque up to the light, sniffs it and puts it in her notebook. "Thank you," she says. "You are the first people in this village to bring me something instead of hiding it. I shall remember that." The village, which saw the estate's carriage at the police station, will remember it too.
La polizia del villaggio è una donna sol.short: Inspector Nell Haskett takes the cheque: "You are the first to bring me something instead of hiding it. I shall remember."

**NOTIZIE DALLA COLLINA.** Proseguono i.easy: **NEWS FROM THE HILL.** Work goes on at Lady Carew's new asylum. The foreman says the roof will be ready before winter. In the paupers' ward, for the first time in the county, each cell will have a window. A small one, but a window.
**NOTIZIE DALLA COLLINA.** Proseguono i.short: **NEWS FROM THE HILL.** The asylum will have its roof before winter, and a small window in every paupers' cell.

Tra i benefattori che hanno contribuito.easy: Lady Carew publicly thanked, among those who paid for the roof, the family from the estate, "who understood before others how important it is to treat things early". The family's name will be written on a brass plaque at the entrance.
Tra i benefattori che hanno contribuito.short: Lady Carew publicly thanks the family from the estate. Their name will go on a plaque at the entrance.

Lady Carew ha voluto ricordare, nel suo.easy: In her speech to the committee Lady Carew said that "certain families of the county prefer to keep their sick at home, until it is too late". She named no names. But everyone turned to look towards the estate on the hill.
Lady Carew ha voluto ricordare, nel suo.short: Lady Carew speaks of families who keep their sick at home "until it is too late". Everyone looks towards the estate.

Il custode del cimitero segnala che da q.easy: The cemetery keeper says that for some time, every morning, there have been fresh violets on the grave of the old man from the estate. And that an heir of the family has been seen walking among the graves in the middle of the night. This newspaper will say no more.
Il custode del cimitero segnala che da q.short: Every morning there are fresh violets on the old man's grave. And an heir has been seen at the cemetery at night.

Si è chiusa intanto, senza incidenti, la.easy: Meanwhile the protest of the building-site bricklayers, who had gone without pay for six weeks, has ended without trouble. How it ended, the union would rather not say.
Si è chiusa intanto, senza incidenti, la.short: The bricklayers' protest is over. The union will not say how.

Una lavandaia del villaggio racconta che.easy: A village washerwoman says that her son was given, in the Park, a cheque folded like a little boat, signed with the name of an heir from the estate. The family, when we asked, would not answer.
Una lavandaia del villaggio racconta che.short: A child was given a cheque signed by an heir from the estate. The family says nothing.

All'osteria, la sera, si parla poco d'al.easy: At the tavern, in the evening, people talk about almost nothing but Mr. Umber and the estate. From the pulpit the priest asked people not to listen to gossip. So, of course, the gossip doubled.
All'osteria, la sera, si parla poco d'al.short: The tavern talks only of Umber. The priest begs people to ignore the gossip, which doubles.

Per il resto, il villaggio è tranquillo..easy: Otherwise the village is quiet. The harvest was good, the river did not flood, and this year the man in the black coat has not been seen much.
Per il resto, il villaggio è tranquillo..short: Otherwise all is quiet. The man in black has been seen little this year.

Il negoziante ti fa entrare nel retrobot.easy: The shopkeeper takes you into the back room, away from the customers. He has a cheque: it has the name of one of your relatives, the writing slants backwards, and the bank stamp is real. A little man in black brought it last night, in the fog, and bought every candle in the shop and lit them, one by one, on the pavement.
Il negoziante ti fa entrare nel retrobot.short: The shopkeeper has a cheque with a relative's name, in a backward hand. A little man in black brought it and lit every candle on the pavement.

Il bottegaio ti aspetta sulla porta, con.easy: The shopkeeper is waiting at the door, like someone who has prepared a speech. He is holding a cheque: the amount is small, it has the name of one of your relatives, and the writing slants backwards. Last night a little man in a black coat cashed it, paid for a bottle of wine and smashed it on the pavement to hear the noise.
Il bottegaio ti aspetta sulla porta, con.short: The shopkeeper has a cheque with a relative's name, in a backward hand. A little man in black brought it and smashed a bottle to hear it break.

Non vuole storie: vuole i suoi soldi. Op.easy: He does not want trouble: he wants his money. Or, if you prefer, he can tell the police everything.
Non vuole storie: vuole i suoi soldi. Op.short: He wants his money. Or he goes to the police.

Le impronte nel fango sono piccole e sve.easy: The footprints in the mud are small and quick, and all go the same way. You follow them past the market, past the bridge, to the alley behind the estate. There they stop in front of a wooden door with no handle and no lock.
Le impronte nel fango sono piccole e sve.short: You follow the prints to the alley behind the estate. They stop at a door with no handle.

Hai in tasca la chiave dell'apprendista,.easy: In your pocket is the apprentice's key, the one with the eye-shaped head. There is no keyhole to put it in; but when you hold it near the wood, something on the other side clicks, and the door opens.
Hai in tasca la chiave dell'apprendista,.short: You hold the apprentice's key to the wood. Something clicks, and the door opens.

Quando la tocchi, si apre: qualcuno, dal.easy: You touch it, and it opens: someone on the other side forgot to lock it.
Quando la tocchi, si apre: qualcuno, dal.short: The door opens: someone forgot to lock it.

Dietro c'è lo studio sul vicolo, quello.easy: Behind it is the study on the alley, the one in the will: a room none of you had ever managed to find. The walls are covered with mirrors, and there is another door, this one with a handle, that opens into the estate's corridor. It is a house with two doors. Through one comes a respectable scientist; through the other goes whoever likes.
Dietro c'è lo studio sul vicolo, quello.short: It is the study from the will, full of mirrors, with a second door into the estate. A house with two doors.

Il piccolo uomo con il cappotto nero, al.easy: The little man in the black coat on the street corner is a boy in his grandfather's coat and a paper hat. He is pretending to be Umber to scare his sisters, and doing it very well. When he sees you, he runs off laughing.
Il piccolo uomo con il cappotto nero, al.short: It is only a boy in his grandfather's coat, playing at Umber.

Lo trovi dove ti avevano detto: un cappo.easy: You find it where they said: a black coat hung on a fence to dry, with the collar up and a broom handle for shoulders. From far away, in the fog, it really looked like a man waiting for someone.
Lo trovi dove ti avevano detto: un cappo.short: It is only a black coat hung on a fence to dry.

È un ubriaco, addormentato su un gradino.easy: It is a drunk asleep on a doorstep, wearing a black coat that is not his. When you wake him he swears a very kind little gentleman gave it to him, laughing a lot, in exchange for a song.
È un ubriaco, addormentato su un gradino.short: It is a drunk in a black coat, given to him by a little gentleman for a song.

Non c'è nessuno: solo un gatto nero che.easy: There is no one, only a black cat looking for food in the rubbish. But on the ground is a wax seal, with the mark of a crest you think you have seen before.
Non c'è nessuno: solo un gatto nero che.short: Only a black cat. On the ground, a wax seal you think you know.

Nella nebbia, sotto un lampione, un picc.easy: In the fog, under a street lamp, a little man in a black coat is waiting without moving. You go closer slowly. It is a tailor's dummy, stolen from a shop window and put there as a joke by some students. Round its neck is a sign: *You have wasted your time.*
Nella nebbia, sotto un lampione, un picc.short: It is a stolen tailor's dummy, with a sign: *You have wasted your time.*

È un vagabondo basso di statura, che le.easy: It is a short tramp whom Ada Haskett's constables have already stopped twice. Now he enjoys it: he walks about at night in a black coat bought specially, and gets arrested to have a warm bed in a cell.
È un vagabondo basso di statura, che le.short: It is a tramp who wears a black coat to get arrested and sleep somewhere warm.

L'ombra che hai visto scivolare lungo il.easy: The shadow you saw going along the wall is a lamplighter, small and quick, with his ladder on his shoulder and his pole in his hand. He says hello politely. He says he has never seen Umber, and he seems very sorry about it.
L'ombra che hai visto scivolare lungo il.short: It is a lamplighter, small and quick. He has never seen Umber, and is sorry.

Non c'è nessuno, ma sul muro, all'altezz.easy: There is no one. But on the wall, at eye level, someone has drawn a little man with a hat in chalk. Below it is an arrow pointing to the alley you came from.
Non c'è nessuno, ma sul muro, all'altezz.short: No one. On the wall, a chalk little man and an arrow towards your alley.

L'Ispettore Nell Haskett, la prima donna.easy: Inspector Nell Haskett, the first woman with that rank in the whole county, has opened a file on Umber's cheques. She goes from shop to shop with a black notebook and a pencil that is always sharp, and writes everything down: even what you do not tell her.
L'Ispettore Nell Haskett, la prima donna.short: Inspector Nell Haskett is investigating Umber's cheques, and writes everything down: even what you do not say.

L'ufficio dell'Ispettore Haskett è una s.easy: Inspector Haskett's office is a narrow room on the ground floor of the town hall, with a stove that does not warm and a portrait of the king hanging crooked. She has you sit down, offers you a tea you do not drink and puts on the table, side by side, six cheques with your family's names on them.
L'ufficio dell'Ispettore Haskett è una s.short: The Inspector has you sit, and lays out six cheques bearing your family's names.

\"Non vi accuso di niente\", dice. \"Vor.easy: "I am not accusing you of anything," she says. "I would just like to know who, in your house, goes out at night."
\"Non vi accuso di niente\", dice. \"Vor.short: "I would just like to know who, in your house, goes out at night."

Racconti delle boccette, del biglietto d.easy: You tell her about the phials, your father's note, the first sip. The Inspector listens without interrupting and without writing, and when you have finished she is quiet for a long time. Then she closes her notebook. "I cannot arrest a salt," she says. "But from today I know where to look. And I know I can trust at least one of you."
Racconti delle boccette, del biglietto d.short: You tell her about the salt. "I cannot arrest a salt," she says. "But I know where to look, and whom to trust."

Dici che alla tenuta si va a letto prest.easy: You say that at the estate everyone goes to bed early, that the laboratory is locked and that the cheques must be forged. At every sentence the Inspector nods kindly and writes a word in her notebook. At the end she walks you to the door and wishes you good night, rather pointedly.
Dici che alla tenuta si va a letto prest.short: You say everyone sleeps at the estate. The Inspector nods and writes. Then she wishes you good night, pointedly.

Fai un nome. Non è il tuo. L'Ispettore l.easy: You say a name. Not yours. The Inspector writes it in capitals, underlines it twice and thanks you for your help. Then she looks at you the way you look at a dog that has brought a dead rat into the house. On your way back to the estate you meet the relative you named. They say hello. They know nothing yet.
Fai un nome. Non è il tuo. L'Ispettore l.short: You name a relative. The Inspector writes it down, and looks at you with contempt. In the street the relative greets you. They know nothing.

Il farmacista Lomax ha il suo banco tra.easy: Lomax the chemist has his stall between the chicken cages and the wheels of cheese: cough syrups, liver pills, salts for every occasion. He is a thin man, still young, with yellow fingers and the look of someone who has been waiting years for bad news.
Il farmacista Lomax ha il suo banco tra.short: Lomax the chemist, thin and yellow-fingered, has a market stall. He seems to have been expecting bad news for years.

Quando gli chiedi della prima partita di.easy: When you ask him about the first batch of salt he sold your father he goes pale and says he does not remember: he has sold lots of salt to lots of people. But he keeps his hand on his ledger, as if it might run away.
Quando gli chiedi della prima partita di.short: You ask about the first batch of salt. He says he does not remember, but keeps his hand on his ledger.

Lomax guarda il denaro, poi la folla, po.easy: Lomax looks at the money, then at the people, then at the money again. He tears a page from the ledger and gives it to you folded in four. *9 November 1859: six phials, white salt, delivered to the gentleman at the estate.* In the ingredients column, next to the salt, is a line crossed out so hard that the ink has gone through the paper.
Lomax guarda il denaro, poi la folla, po.short: Lomax sells you the page: *9 November 1859: six phials, white salt.* Beside the salt, a line crossed out so hard it tore the paper.

Lo prendi per il bavero davanti a tutto.easy: You grab him by the collar in front of the whole market. The hens squawk, a cheese rolls into the mud, and someone runs to get the Inspector. Lomax says nothing. He puts a phial of salt in your hand, "the best I have", and begs you to leave. That evening, in the glass, the salt turns only slightly red, and that is all.
Lo prendi per il bavero davanti a tutto.short: You grab him by the collar. Lomax says nothing: he gives you a phial of salt that barely turns red.

Lomax te la incarta con cura e non ti fa.easy: Lomax wraps it carefully and does not even make you pay. "Salt from the second batch," he says. "Very pure. Your father bought kilos of it, later. He never liked it." You try it that evening, in a glass of water: it turns red and stops. Nothing happens. And for some reason, that seems to you the worst news of all.
Lomax te la incarta con cura e non ti fa.short: "Salt from the second batch. Very pure." In the glass it turns red and stops. Nothing happens.

L'apprendista del fabbro è un ragazzo co.easy: The blacksmith's apprentice is a boy with arms black up to the elbows who loves to talk. While he works he tells you that last month a little gentleman in a black coat ordered a strange key: no teeth, with an eye-shaped head, "for a door that opens only from the inside". He paid with a cheque. The boy kept the mould, just in case.
L'apprendista del fabbro è un ragazzo co.short: The apprentice made a toothless key for a little gentleman in black, "for a door that opens only from the inside". He kept the mould.

Il ragazzo ci mette tutto il pomeriggio..easy: It takes the boy all afternoon. The key he gives you is still warm, heavy, and useless: there is no lock in the world it would fit. And yet, when you hold it tight, it seems to pull gently towards the alley behind the estate, like a compass needle.
Il ragazzo ci mette tutto il pomeriggio..short: The key fits no lock. But it pulls gently towards the alley behind the estate, like a compass.

L'Ispettore sequestra lo stampo e ringra.easy: The Inspector takes the mould and thanks you. The boy spends a night in a cell and comes out with a black eye and a very bad opinion of your family. Three days later the mould disappears from the police store.
L'Ispettore sequestra lo stampo e ringra.short: The Inspector seizes the mould. Three days later, it vanishes.

Lasci il ragazzo alle sue chiacchiere e.easy: You leave the boy to his chatter and his anvil. On the way home you go through the alley behind the estate without meaning to, and without meaning to you look for a door with no handle. You do not see it. But that does not mean it is not there.
Lasci il ragazzo alle sue chiacchiere e.short: On your way back you pass the alley and look for a handleless door. You do not see it. That does not mean it is not there.

**IL NUOVO MANICOMIO APRE LE PORTE.** Ie.easy: **THE NEW ASYLUM OPENS ITS DOORS.** Yesterday morning, with the bishop and the most important families of the county, Lady Carew opened the asylum on the hill. There are a hundred beds, hot water on every floor, gardens for walking and a ward for gentlefolk, kept apart from the paupers' ward by a wall four metres high.
**IL NUOVO MANICOMIO APRE LE PORTE.** Ie.short: **THE NEW ASYLUM OPENS ITS DOORS.** A hundred beds, hot water, gardens and a ward for gentlefolk, walled off from the poor.

Nel suo discorso Lady Carew ha invitato.easy: In her speech Lady Carew told respectable families not to be ashamed. Madness, she said, is not a fault but an illness, and it is easier to cure if you catch it early. Anyone with a relative at home who sleeps little, goes out at night or sees things others do not see must report it.
Nel suo discorso Lady Carew ha invitato.short: Lady Carew asks families to report anyone who sleeps little, goes out at night or sees strange things.

Questo giornale ha appreso che la prima.easy: This newspaper knows that the first report has already arrived, unsigned, and is about one of the heirs of the estate. The letter is written in small handwriting that slants backwards.
Questo giornale ha appreso che la prima.short: The first report, unsigned, names an heir of the estate. The handwriting slants backwards.

Lady Carew, che ha il nome della famigli.easy: Lady Carew, who has the family's name on a plaque at the entrance, said that anyone who is reported will get the best care, in the gentlefolk's ward.
Lady Carew, che ha il nome della famigli.short: Lady Carew promises the best care, in the gentlefolk's ward, to anyone reported.

Lady Carew ha aggiunto che certe famigli.easy: Lady Carew also said that certain families "with no need of asylums" should remember that the asylum, however, needs them.
Lady Carew ha aggiunto che certe famigli.short: Lady Carew notes that the asylum needs certain families, even if they do not need it.

La carrozza del manicomio arriva al matt.easy: The asylum carriage arrives early in the morning, with two attendants in white aprons and a form ready to sign. The family signs without looking at each other. Lady Carew, who wanted to escort her first important patient herself, thanks everyone for doing their duty. And for a few months the village stops talking about the estate.
La carrozza del manicomio arriva al matt.short: The family signs, and the asylum carriage takes an heir away. For a few months the village is silent.

La famiglia chiude il cancello e non ris.easy: The family shuts the gate and does not answer letters. Lady Carew drives past the estate twice without stopping. The third time she stops, looks for a long time at the laboratory windows and writes something in her leather notebook. In the village they say the people at the estate have something to hide. And for once they are right.
La famiglia chiude il cancello e non ris.short: The family shuts the gate. Lady Carew drives by, studies the laboratory and writes in her notebook. The village says you have something to hide. It is right.

Cara Margaret, ti scrivo dal mio ufficio.easy: Dear Margaret, I am writing from my office, with the stove out because the council will not pay for wood. The Umber case keeps me awake. For thirteen years I have been collecting cheques in the same handwriting, and for thirteen years that family has smiled at me on its doorstep.
Cara Margaret, ti scrivo dal mio ufficio.short: Dear Margaret, the Umber case keeps me awake. For thirteen years I have collected cheques in the same hand, and that family smiles at me.

Devo dire che non tutti mi mentono. Qual.easy: I must say not all of them lie to me. Someone up at the estate has told me the truth more than once, even when it cost them. I do not know if it is courage or tiredness. Either way, I remember it.
Devo dire che non tutti mi mentono. Qual.short: Someone at the estate has told me the truth, even when it cost them. I remember it.

Mi mentono tutti, lassù, con una cortesi.easy: Up there they all lie to me, so politely that I want to arrest them on principle. I have learned to tell when they are lying by the way they straighten their cuffs.
Mi mentono tutti, lassù, con una cortesi.short: They all lie to me, politely. I can tell by how they straighten their cuffs.

Ho saputo che uno di loro ha comprato un.easy: I heard that one of them bought a page of Lomax the chemist's ledger, at the market, in front of half the village. I do not know what was on it. Since then Lomax has closed his shop at six.
Ho saputo che uno di loro ha comprato un.short: One of them bought a page of Lomax's ledger. Since then Lomax closes at six.

Uno di loro ha preso per il bavero il fa.easy: One of them grabbed Lomax the chemist by the collar in the middle of the market. Lomax would not report it. A man who will not report it, Margaret, is afraid of something worse than the police.
Uno di loro ha preso per il bavero il fa.short: One of them attacked Lomax at the market. Lomax will not report it: he fears something worse than the police.

L'apprendista del fabbro mi ha raccontat.easy: The blacksmith's apprentice, after two beers, told me about a toothless key made for a little gentleman, and a copy made for the estate. I looked for the door it opens. I did not find it. I think the door has to find me.
L'apprendista del fabbro mi ha raccontat.short: The apprentice made a toothless key, and a copy for the estate. I cannot find the door it opens.

Il mese scorso un ufficiale in congedo h.easy: Last month an officer challenged an heir of the estate to a duel, because of an insult from a little man in a black coat at the tavern. It ended with no one hurt. You can imagine the rest: the village talked of nothing else for weeks.
Il mese scorso un ufficiale in congedo h.short: An officer challenged an heir to a duel over the man in black's insult. No one was hurt, but the village talks of nothing else.

Uno degli eredi è stato internato nel ma.easy: One of the heirs has been shut away in Lady Carew's asylum, in the gentlefolk's ward. The family signed without arguing. But the cheques have not become fewer.
Uno degli eredi è stato internato nel ma.short: An heir has been committed. The cheques have not grown fewer.

Domani scrivo alla capitale per chiedere.easy: Tomorrow I am writing to the capital to ask for a handwriting expert. If they send the one I hope for, in a few years we shall at least know who writes those cheques. I am afraid I know already. Give my love to the children. Yours, Nell.
Domani scrivo alla capitale per chiedere.short: I shall ask for a handwriting expert. I fear I already know who writes the cheques. Yours, Nell.

L'Ispettore Haskett ha fatto venire dall.easy: Inspector Haskett has brought a handwriting expert from the capital, a little man with thick glasses and a case full of lenses. He has asked the family for a letter from each of them, and to see the father's Journal, at the estate, in front of the notary.
L'Ispettore Haskett ha fatto venire dall.short: The handwriting expert has arrived. He wants a letter from each of you and the father's Journal.

La fucina è chiusa, ma dentro c'è luce..easy: The forge is closed, but there is a light inside. The blacksmith is asleep on his bench, his head in his arms. By the fire, sitting on an anvil like a throne, is a little man in a black coat that is too big for him. He is warming his hands, and he smiles at you as if he had been waiting for you for years.
La fucina è chiusa, ma dentro c'è luce..short: In the forge, sitting on an anvil, is a little man in black. He smiles, as if he had been waiting for you.

\"Finalmente qualcuno di famiglia\", dic.easy: "Someone from the family at last," he says. He has a young voice and an old laugh. From his pocket he takes a page torn from the Journal, full of formulas. "This is yours. You can have it if you sign a blank cheque, with your name. It won't cost you anything. Not right away."
\"Finalmente qualcuno di famiglia\", dic.short: "Family at last." He offers you a page of the Journal in exchange for a blank cheque with your signature.

Firmi, con la mano che trema. Umber soff.easy: You sign, with a shaking hand. Umber blows on the ink, folds the cheque and puts it in his breast pocket, near his heart. The page he gives you is in your father's handwriting, the upright, respectable one, and it is the most beautiful thing you have ever read. When you look up, there is no one on the anvil.
Firmi, con la mano che trema. Umber soff.short: You sign. The page is in your father's hand, and beautiful. When you look up, Umber is gone.

Gli salti addosso. È leggero come un bam.easy: You jump at him. He is as light as a child and as quick as a cat: he slips out of your arms, leaves you holding his empty coat and runs off into the alley laughing. The pockets are empty. There is only a smell, and you know it: sweet tobacco and laboratory acid. The smell of your father.
Gli salti addosso. È leggero come un bam.short: He slips away and leaves you his coat. It smells of your father.

Quando torni con le guardie, le lanterne.easy: When you come back with the constables, their lanterns and sticks, the forge is dark and the blacksmith is snoring on his bench. On the anvil there is only a cheque for a penny, made out to you, "for your trouble". The constables laugh all the way back. Inspector Haskett does not: she takes the cheque and puts it in her notebook.
Quando torni con le guardie, le lanterne.short: The constables find only a penny cheque for you. They laugh. Inspector Haskett does not.

Il reparto dei signori ha i tappeti, le.easy: The gentlefolk's ward has carpets, velvet curtains and bars painted white so they look like picture frames. Your relative sits by the window in a dressing gown, writing letters they never send. They greet you kindly, the way one greets a stranger. They are writing with their left hand.
Il reparto dei signori ha i tappeti, le.short: Your committed relative greets you like a stranger. They write letters with their left hand.

Lady Carew ti accompagna nella visita di.easy: Lady Carew shows you round herself. When someone calls her into the corridor, she leaves her leather notebook on the desk, open.
Lady Carew ti accompagna nella visita di.short: Lady Carew steps out and leaves her notebook open on the desk.

Sono pagine di nomi, e accanto a ogni no.easy: There are pages of names, and next to each name an illness and an amount. Your relative's name is there too, underlined: *interesting case*. At the back, on a separate page, are the accounts of the gentlefolk's ward. Respectable families do not pay for the asylum. For seven years it has been paid by a cheque every month, always the same amount, always with the same signature: *Umber*.
Sono pagine di nomi, e accanto a ogni no.short: Your relative is marked *interesting case*. And for seven years the gentlefolk's ward has been paid for by Umber.

Quando Lady Carew rientra, il libretto è.easy: When Lady Carew comes back, the notebook is closed, exactly where she left it. She smiles at you. You smile at her. Neither of you believes it.
Quando Lady Carew rientra, il libretto è.short: Lady Carew returns and smiles. You smile. Neither of you believes it.

L'infermiere conta le monete senza vergo.easy: The attendant counts the coins without shame. That evening your relative comes back to the estate in a hired carriage, dressing gown under their coat, and asks straight away about the laboratory. At dinner they hold their fork in their right hand, as always. Almost always.
L'infermiere conta le monete senza vergo.short: You pay the attendant, and your relative comes home. At dinner they hold the fork in their right hand. Almost always.

Lady Carew vede la moneta cadere nella c.easy: Lady Carew sees the coin fall into the box and thanks you with a nod, the way you thank someone who has understood the rules. Before saying goodbye she promises your relative will be treated very well. She says it looking at her notebook.
Lady Carew vede la moneta cadere nella c.short: Lady Carew thanks you, and promises your relative will be well treated. She says it looking at her notebook.

È notte, e sulla tomba del padre c'è una.easy: It is night, and there is a lantern on your father's grave. Silas Pell the notary is standing in front of the headstone, alone, holding his hat. He has grown much older in these years. You see him take a small paper packet from his waistcoat and sprinkle a pinch of grey powder on the grave, carefully, the way you salt soup.
È notte, e sulla tomba del padre c'è una.short: At night, on your father's grave, Silas Pell the notary sprinkles a pinch of grey powder.

\"Ci siamo cascati tutti e due, vecchio.easy: "We both fell for it, old friend," he says to the headstone. "You over there. Me over here."
\"Ci siamo cascati tutti e due, vecchio.short: "We both fell for it, old friend. You over there. Me over here."

Il notaio trasale, e la lanterna gli tre.easy: The notary jumps, and the lantern shakes in his hand. For a moment he seems about to tell you everything. Then he puts his hat back on. "Your father wrote many things," he says. "Not all of them true, and none of them for you. My cupboard is locked, and I have the key. Make sure it stays that way." He leaves without saying good night.
Il notaio trasale, e la lanterna gli tre.short: The notary almost tells you everything, then thinks better of it: "My cupboard is locked, and I have the key. Keep it that way."

Aspetti che la lanterna sparisca oltre i.easy: You wait for the lantern to disappear past the gate, then gather the grey powder from the headstone with a handkerchief. It tastes of nothing. In the laboratory you dissolve a pinch in a glass with salt from Lomax's second batch: the colour turns red, then violet, and stops there, as if something were still missing. Or as if there were too little of it.
Aspetti che la lanterna sparisca oltre i.short: You gather the grey powder. With Lomax's salt the colour reaches violet, and stops. Something is still missing.

Torni indietro piano, tra le lapidi, sen.easy: You go back quietly, among the graves, without a sound. Behind you the notary goes on talking softly to the grave, for a long time. Just once, it seems to you, the grave answers him. But perhaps it is the wind, or an owl, or your imagination.
Torni indietro piano, tra le lapidi, sen.short: You slip away. Once, it seems, the grave answers the notary.

Come da Vostra richiesta, il sottoscritt.easy: As you asked, I have examined the twenty-three cheques collected from the village shops over the last sixteen years, signed with different names. I have compared them with the letters of the heirs of the estate and with the Journal of their dead father.
Come da Vostra richiesta, il sottoscritt.short: I compared twenty-three cheques from sixteen years with the heirs' letters and their father's Journal.

Le conclusioni sono le seguenti. Primo:.easy: Here are the conclusions. First: all the cheques were written by the same hand. Second: that hand does not belong to any of the heirs, whose writing is, for this report, surprisingly innocent. Third: that hand is the same as the Journal's.
Le conclusioni sono le seguenti. Primo:.short: All the cheques are in one hand. Not the heirs'. It is the Journal's.

La pressione della penna, la *g* chiusa.easy: The pressure of the pen, the *g* closed like a knot, the signature going up to the right: everything is the same, except the slant. In the Journal the writing leans forward, like any respectable person's; in the cheques it leans backwards. I have seen something like it only once, in a man who learned to write with his left hand after losing his right.
La pressione della penna, la *g* chiusa.short: Everything matches but the slant: in the Journal the writing leans forward, in the cheques backwards.

Il sottoscritto segnala un'eccezione. Tr.easy: I report one exception. Among the newest cheques is one filled in by the usual hand, but really signed by an heir, in their own writing and with their own slant. Someone in the family has signed for him.
Il sottoscritto segnala un'eccezione. Tr.short: One recent cheque is truly signed by an heir. Someone in the family signed for him.

Il sottoscritto aggiunge, senza che gli.easy: I add, though nobody asked me, that one of the cheques is dated last week.
Il sottoscritto aggiunge, senza che gli.short: One of the cheques is from last week.

Alle due di notte, con l'autorizzazione.easy: At two in the morning, with the judge's permission and in front of the heirs and Silas Pell the notary, we had the dead man's grave opened. The notary was against it to the end; then he signed, and looked the other way.
Alle due di notte, con l'autorizzazione.short: At two in the morning we opened the grave. Pell the notary refused; then he signed, looking away.

La bara era intatta, chiusa con i chiodi.easy: The coffin was whole, closed with the carpenter's nails. Inside, wrapped in a sheet with the family's initials, were river stones: about seventy kilograms. On top of the stones was a cheque folded in four, signed *Umber*, with a note in the same slanting writing: *The notary was right: the circumstances were not doubtful. They were false.*
La bara era intatta, chiusa con i chiodi.short: The coffin held only river stones. And a note from Umber: *The circumstances were not doubtful. They were false.*

Il parroco, presente all'apertura, si è.easy: The priest, who was there, crossed himself and said only: "It weighed like a stone. I told him so."
Il parroco, presente all'apertura, si è.short: The priest crossed himself: "It weighed like a stone. I told him so."

Uno degli eredi, che anni fa aveva passa.easy: One of the heirs, who spent a night in this cemetery years ago, recognised in the mud around the grave the same footprints as back then: small, quick, fresh.
Uno degli eredi, che anni fa aveva passa.short: An heir recognised the footprints from years ago in the mud: small, and fresh.

Il medico condotto, interrogato all'alba.easy: The village doctor, questioned at dawn, admitted he signed the death certificate without seeing the body. He was paid with a cheque.
Il medico condotto, interrogato all'alba.short: The doctor signed the death certificate without seeing the body. He was paid with a cheque.

L'Ispettore Haskett vi lascia una notte.easy: Inspector Haskett gives you one night to decide, and puts two constables at the gate. She remembers every lie you have told her. Without the Journal she has no proof that will stand up in court: a handwriting, a coffin of stones, a doctor who changed his story. With the Journal, she can have a dead man arrested.
L'Ispettore Haskett vi lascia una notte.short: The Inspector gives you a night, with two constables at the gate. Without the Journal she has no proof. With it, she can arrest a dead man.

L'Ispettore Haskett vi lascia una notte.easy: Inspector Haskett gives you one night to decide. Without the Journal she has no proof that will stand up in court: a handwriting, a coffin of stones, a doctor who changed his story. With the Journal, she can have a dead man arrested.
