L'Ispettore Haskett vi lascia una notte.short: The Inspector gives you a night. Without the Journal she has no proof. With it, she can arrest a dead man.

Prima di andarsene vi stringe la mano, a.easy: Before she leaves she shakes your hands, one by one. "I asked you for the truth, and you told me," she says. "Whatever you decide, I shall not forget it."
Prima di andarsene vi stringe la mano, a.short: She shakes your hands: "You told me the truth. I shall not forget it."

Le pietre di fiume tornano al fiume. La.easy: The river stones go back to the river. The empty coffin stays in the open grave for three days, in the rain, until the cemetery keeper asks the family what to do with it. The headstone, with the father's name and the two dates, is still there. But now one of the two dates is a lie.
Le pietre di fiume tornano al fiume. La.short: The empty coffin lies in the open grave. On the headstone, one of the two dates is now a lie.

Il custode richiude la fossa e rimette a.easy: The keeper fills in the grave and puts the headstone back. For the village the father is dead, and stays dead. The next morning the violets are there again.
Il custode richiude la fossa e rimette a.short: The keeper closes the grave. The next day the violets are back.

Lo scalpellino cancella il nome a colpi.easy: The stonemason hammers the name away, one letter at a time. What is left is a smooth stone with two dates and a cross. The village approves: a man who is not dead has no right to a grave. The next morning the violets are gone.
Lo scalpellino cancella il nome a colpi.short: The name is chiselled away. The next day the violets are gone.

Lo scalpellino incide le due parole sott.easy: The stonemason carves the three words under the name, in smaller letters, and asks twice if he has understood correctly. The village thinks it is in very bad taste. The next morning, on the grave, next to the violets, there is a note: *You can count on it.*
Lo scalpellino incide le due parole sott.short: You have *Come back soon* carved under the name. The next day, among the violets, a note: *You can count on it.*

L'Ispettore Haskett dà la caccia a un mo.easy: Inspector Haskett hunts a dead man for two years. She has his portrait printed on posters all over the county, with WANTED and a reward. But the portrait shows a tall, elegant man, and nobody has ever seen Umber like that. The posters end up wrapping fish.
L'Ispettore Haskett dà la caccia a un mo.short: The Inspector hunts the father for two years. But the posters show a tall, elegant man, and Umber is not like that.

Nell'inverno del 1879, sul ponte, trovan.easy: In the winter of 1879, on the bridge, they find a black coat that is too big, carefully folded, with its pockets full of labels from Lomax's pharmacy. They find nothing else of the father.
Nell'inverno del 1879, sul ponte, trovan.short: In 1879 a folded black coat is found on the bridge. Of the father, nothing.

Il Journal brucia nel caminetto della bi.easy: The Journal burns in the library fireplace, one page at a time, while the Inspector waits in her carriage outside the gate. When the family tells her the notebook was lost years ago, she writes something in her notebook and does not insist.
Il Journal brucia nel caminetto della bi.short: You burn the Journal and tell the Inspector it was lost years ago. She writes something, and lets it go.

L'ultima pagina, sollevata dal calore, v.easy: The last page, lifted by the heat, flies up the chimney before anyone can catch it. The next morning the baker finds it in the gutter and brings it back to the estate. It is blank. But on the back, in the backward-slanting writing, there is a single word: *thank you*.
L'ultima pagina, sollevata dal calore, v.short: The last page flies away. The next day it is back: blank, with one word on the back, slanting backwards: *thank you*.

Gli eredi della prima generazione moriro.easy: The heirs of the first generation died in the years after, all of natural causes, all in their beds. This time my father checked every coffin himself before it was closed. The sightings, however, went on.
Gli eredi della prima generazione moriro.short: The heirs died in their beds, and my father checked every coffin. The sightings went on.

Mio padre chiuse il fascicolo nel 1880,.easy: My father closed the file in 1880, with a note in the margin: *Case closed*. Many years later, underneath, I added: *Not yet.*
Mio padre chiuse il fascicolo nel 1880,.short: My father wrote: *Case closed*. Years later, I added: *Not yet.*

Mio padre è morto due anni fa, con la pe.easy: My father died two years ago, pen in hand, while writing a contract. He left me his practice, his clients, a locked cupboard whose key I have never found, and this file, which I should never have opened again.
Mio padre è morto due anni fa, con la pe.short: My father died two years ago. He left me his practice, a locked cupboard with no key and this file.

Negli ultimi anni mio padre non dormiva.easy: In his last years my father stopped sleeping in his bed. Ever since one of the heirs of the estate went looking for him in the cemetery, at night, to ask him questions, he slept in his office, in an armchair, in front of the cupboard.
Negli ultimi anni mio padre non dormiva.short: After an heir sought him out at the cemetery, my father slept in an armchair, in front of the cupboard.

In venticinque anni il villaggio è diven.easy: In twenty-five years the village has become a town. The wooden houses have fallen one after another, and in their place are houses of grey stone, all the same, with gas lamps outside the door. The train has come, and with the train the soot. Nothing more has been heard of the old man: by law he died in 1861, and no one wants to talk about it again.
In venticinque anni il villaggio è diven.short: The village has become a town of stone, with trains and soot. Nothing more is known of the old man.

Gli avvistamenti di Mr. Umber, invece, n.easy: But the sightings of Mr. Umber have never stopped. A little man in a black coat, not one day older, pays with cheques signed by respectable people and laughs at the end of the street. Today the heirs of the estate are the old man's grandchildren. None of them has ever seen the phials of salt, but they all know where they are.
Gli avvistamenti di Mr. Umber, invece, n.short: But Umber is still seen: not a day older. The heirs are the old man's grandchildren, and know where the phials are.

Sono cresciuti con le storie, come si cr.easy: They grew up with these stories, the way you grow up with bread: the grandfather who was not dead, the coffin full of stones, the door with no handle. At school their friends dared each other to touch the estate's gate. Now those friends are lawyers, doctors, councillors, and they cross the street when they see them.
Sono cresciuti con le storie, come si cr.short: They grew up on stories of their grandfather. Their schoolfriends now cross the street.

Ti svegli prima dell'alba sopra le coper.easy: You wake before dawn on top of the covers, fully dressed. Your shoes are dirty with river mud. In your pocket is a cheque signed with your name, in your hand: but the writing slants backwards. You have never touched the salt. You did not need to: whoever came before you drank it for you. You are Umber. You always were.
Ti svegli prima dell'alba sopra le coper.short: You wake with muddy shoes and a cheque signed by you, slanting backwards. You never drank the salt. You are Umber.

Sogni il vicolo dietro la tenuta, la por.easy: You dream of the alley behind the estate, the door with no handle, and a laugh behind you that you have always known. You wake suddenly, your heart racing. The bed is tidy, your shoes are clean by the door, your pockets empty. And yet, for a moment, you would have sworn your hands were muddy.
Sogni il vicolo dietro la tenuta, la por.short: You dream of the alley and a laugh. You wake: all is in order. But for a moment your hands seem muddy.

In banca il cassiere guarda la firma, gu.easy: At the bank the cashier looks at the signature, then at you, and counts out the money without saying anything.
In banca il cassiere guarda la firma, gu.short: The cashier looks at the signature, and pays.

Nella tasca del cappotto c'è del denaro.easy: In the coat pocket there is some money you do not remember putting there.
Nella tasca del cappotto c'è del denaro.short: In the pocket, money you do not remember.

La carta brucia in fretta, con una fiamm.easy: The paper burns quickly, with a slightly green flame. You feel better, almost.
La carta brucia in fretta, con una fiamm.short: It burns with a green flame. You feel better, almost.

Il sonno arriva subito, profondo e senza.easy: You fall asleep at once, deeply, without dreams. You feel better, almost.
Il sonno arriva subito, profondo e senza.short: You sleep without dreams. You feel better, almost.

Dove c'era il mercato del villaggio, ade.easy: Where the village market used to be there is now the Jail: a red-brick building with barred windows that people call "the new hotel". Half the river has been covered, and carriages drive over it.
Dove c'era il mercato del villaggio, ade.short: Where the market stood is now the Jail, "the new hotel". Half the river is covered.

L'Ispettore Nell Haskett è andata in pen.easy: Inspector Nell Haskett has retired. She lives in a little house near the station, with a cat and her old black notebook. She still gets visits from the person who took her place: her niece, Inspector Ada Haskett, who has the same eyes and an even sharper pencil. The first file Ada opened, on her first day, was Mr. Umber's.
L'Ispettore Nell Haskett è andata in pen.short: Nell Haskett has retired. Her niece, Inspector Ada Haskett, has taken her place. Her first file: Mr. Umber.

Alla tenuta, intanto, arriva un signore.easy: Meanwhile a gentleman from the railway company comes to the estate, with a shiny moustache and a leather case. The new railway line must run along the edge of the estate, right behind the alley. The company offers a good price for that strip of land, and an even better one if the family signs quickly.
Alla tenuta, intanto, arriva un signore.short: The railway wants to buy the land along the alley, and pays well if you sign quickly.

Firmate in fretta, e la compagnia paga i.easy: You sign quickly, and the company pays quickly. A month later the workmen knock down the wall and lay the rails ten metres from the alley. Now goods trains go by at night, and nobody hears anything any more: no footsteps, no laughter.
Firmate in fretta, e la compagnia paga i.short: You sell. Now trains pass at night, and no one hears footsteps or laughter any more.

Rifiutate. Il signore con i baffi cerati.easy: You refuse. The gentleman with the shiny moustache leaves shaking his head. The railway makes a wide curve round the estate, and on the company's maps the estate is marked in grey, like the marshes. In town they say the family is hiding something behind that wall. They are not entirely wrong.
Rifiutate. Il signore con i baffi cerati.short: You refuse. The railway curves round the estate, and the town says you are hiding something. It is not wrong.

Gli assegni di Umber ricompaiono nelle b.easy: Umber's cheques turn up in the shops again, signed with your names. No one in the family says they drank the salt.
Gli assegni di Umber ricompaiono nelle b.short: Umber's cheques return with your names. No one admits to drinking the salt.

La nuova Jail ha il riscaldamento a vapo.easy: The new Jail has steam heating, numbered cells and an office on the first floor with a window onto the yard. Inspector Ada Haskett is young, younger than you expected. She has her aunt's eyes and an even sharper pencil. On the desk there is a single file, as thick as a prayer book. On the cover it says *Umber*.
La nuova Jail ha il riscaldamento a vapo.short: Inspector Ada Haskett is young, with her aunt's eyes. On her desk is a single file: *Umber*.

\"Mia zia mi ha parlato della vostra fam.easy: "My aunt told me about your family," she says, before you can speak. "She says you are people one can talk to. I hope she is right. She usually is."
\"Mia zia mi ha parlato della vostra fam.short: "My aunt says you are people one can talk to. She is usually right."

\"Mia zia mi ha parlato della vostra fam.easy: "My aunt told me about your family," she says, before you can speak. "She told me not to believe anything you tell me. She is usually right."
\"Mia zia mi ha parlato della vostra fam.short: "My aunt says not to believe a word you tell me. She is usually right."

\"Mia zia mi ha parlato della vostra fam.easy: "My aunt told me about your family," she says. "She did not tell me whether to trust you. I think she wanted to leave me the pleasure of finding out myself."
\"Mia zia mi ha parlato della vostra fam.short: "My aunt did not say whether to trust you. I shall find out myself."

Ada ti guarda a lungo, come se cercasse.easy: Ada looks at you for a long time, as if she were looking for the lie. Then she opens a drawer and gives you a brass whistle, like the constables' ones. "If you see him, blow it," she says. "And if one day you have to tell me something you don't like, come to me before I come to you."
Ada ti guarda a lungo, come se cercasse.short: Ada gives you a whistle: "If you see him, blow it. And come to me before I come to you."

Ada sorride. \"Volentieri\", dice. \"Il.easy: Ada smiles. "Gladly," she says. "When Umber leaves the town in peace, I shall leave you in peace." She writes a line in the file, closes it and wishes you a good day. It is the first time "good day" has sounded like a threat.
Ada sorride. \"Volentieri\", dice. \"Il.short: "When Umber leaves the town alone, I shall leave you alone." Her good day sounds like a threat.

Ada conta le monete davanti a te, una pe.easy: Ada counts the coins in front of you, one at a time, and locks them in the drawer labelled *Evidence*. Then she tells you where Umber was last seen, and thanks you: "That goes in the file."
Ada conta le monete davanti a te, una pe.short: Ada locks the coins in the *Evidence* drawer, tells you where Umber was last seen and thanks you.

Si vota per il consiglio comunale, e al.easy: There is an election for the town council, and at the town hall the candidates' posters cover the walls up to the ceiling. One poster has no picture and no programme. There is only a name, *U. Mber*, and a promise: "lamps lit all night, so that everyone can see who walks beside them". The town clerk swears the candidacy is in order: the deposit was paid with a cheque.
Si vota per il consiglio comunale, e al.short: At the election there is a candidate with no picture: *U. Mber*. He promises lamps lit all night. He paid the deposit with a cheque.

Li strappi tutti, uno per uno, davanti a.easy: You tear down every poster, one at a time, in front of the town hall, in broad daylight. A constable watches you and does nothing, then writes something in his notebook. At dawn the posters are back, bigger.
Li strappi tutti, uno per uno, davanti a.short: You tear down the posters. At dawn they are back, bigger.

Fai stampare i manifesti, stringi mani a.easy: You have posters printed, shake hands at the market, promise new drains and less fog. Of course you lose, but with honour. *U. Mber* gets just one vote, and no one knows who cast it: the teller swears he counted three times. And yet on the evening of the count, at the town hall, someone laughs for a whole hour.
Fai stampare i manifesti, stringi mani a.short: You stand and lose with honour. *U. Mber* gets one vote. That evening, at the town hall, someone laughs for an hour.

Nella cabina scrivi il suo nome con la t.easy: In the booth you write his name with your pencil, in your handwriting. Halfway through you notice the letters are slanting backwards. When you come out, the teller wishes you good night by your first name, though you have never met.
Nella cabina scrivi il suo nome con la t.short: You vote for him, and your letters slant backwards. The teller, a stranger, calls you by name.

Sulla tomba del nonno, sotto il nome, le.easy: On your grandfather's grave, under the name, you can still read the words your parents had carved: *Come back soon*. Someone has gone over them with a chisel recently: the grooves are white and clean. In front of the headstone are the usual violets.
Sulla tomba del nonno, sotto il nome, le.short: Under your grandfather's name, *Come back soon* has been recut. And the usual violets are there.

La lapide senza nome del nonno è coperta.easy: Your grandfather's nameless headstone is covered in moss, except in one place. Where the name used to be, someone has scraped off the moss with a fingernail, one letter at a time, and the name can be read again, green on grey. In front of the headstone, after so many years, the violets have come back.
La lapide senza nome del nonno è coperta.short: Someone has scraped your grandfather's name back into the moss. And the violets have come back.

La tomba del nonno è come la lasciarono.easy: Your grandfather's grave is as your parents left it: the name, the two dates, a cross. Every now and then the earth in front is disturbed, as if someone slept on it. In front of the headstone are the usual violets.
La tomba del nonno è come la lasciarono.short: The earth before your grandfather's grave is sometimes disturbed. And the usual violets are there.

Il custode sorveglia per sei notti e non.easy: The keeper keeps watch for six nights and sees nothing. On the seventh he falls asleep. In the morning the violets are fresh, and on his hat, leaning against the headstone, there is a cheque: a week's wages, "for your kindness".
Il custode sorveglia per sei notti e non.short: The keeper watches six nights. On the seventh he dozes, and finds a cheque on his hat, "for your kindness".

Scrivi poche righe: *Chi sei? Che cosa v.easy: You write a few lines: *Who are you? What do you want?* The next day the note is gone. In its place there is another, in the backward-slanting hand: *I am family. I want what you want.*
Scrivi poche righe: *Chi sei? Che cosa v.short: *Who are you? What do you want?* The answer: *I am family. I want what you want.*

La chiave senza denti, quella con la tes.easy: The toothless key, the one with the eye-shaped head, has lain for twenty years at the bottom of a drawer. When you pick it up it is warm, and it pulls: gently, patiently, towards the back of the house and the alley, like a compass needle. At night, in the silence, you can even hear a faint hum.
La chiave senza denti, quella con la tes.short: The toothless key is warm, and pulls towards the alley like a compass. At night it hums.

La chiave ti porta lungo il corridoio, g.easy: The key leads you down the corridor and the service stairs, to a wall with no door. You hold it against the wall, and the wall opens: it is the study of mirrors. At the desk, back turned, someone is writing, the pen scratching the paper. They wear a black coat. They do not turn round. You do not stay to see who it is.
La chiave ti porta lungo il corridoio, g.short: The key opens a wall: the study of mirrors. At the desk, back turned, someone in a black coat writes. You leave.

La butti dal ponte, di giorno, davanti a.easy: You throw it off the bridge, in daylight, in front of everyone. It sinks at once, without a sound. That night you sleep as you have not slept for years. The next morning, on your bedside table, there is a small puddle of river water in the shape of a key.
La butti dal ponte, di giorno, davanti a.short: You throw it in the river. Next morning, on your bedside table, there is a puddle shaped like a key.

Gli operai della ferrovia sono in sciope.easy: The railway workers have been on strike for three weeks. The union meets in a smoky room above a tavern, with odd chairs and the crooked portrait of an old bearded union man. The strike should have ended long ago, because the workers have no money left. And yet they hold out. Every Friday someone pays their week's wages, with a cheque.
Gli operai della ferrovia sono in sciope.short: The railway strike has lasted three weeks. The workers hold out because every Friday someone pays them by cheque.

Gli operai ti applaudono, il segretario.easy: The workers clap, and the union secretary shakes your hand with his coal-black hands. For a week, in town, the family at the estate is "the one that stands with the workers". The gentlemen at the club will not forgive you. The workers will not forget it.
Gli operai ti applaudono, il segretario.short: The workers cheer. The club will not forgive you; the workers will not forget.

Il segretario esita, poi ti mostra l'ass.easy: The secretary hesitates, then shows you last Friday's cheque. It is made out to the union and signed with the name of one of you, in the backward-slanting hand. On the back, in pencil, someone has written: *Hold out. It's good for your health.*
Il segretario esita, poi ti mostra l'ass.short: The cheque bears one of your names, slanting backwards. On the back: *Hold out. It's good for your health.*

La compagnia ringrazia e fa bloccare gli.easy: The company thanks you and has the cheques stopped at the bank. The strike ends in a week, because the workers are hungry. That same night, on the estate wall, someone writes in charcoal: *UMBER'S SPY*.
La compagnia ringrazia e fa bloccare gli.short: The cheques are stopped and the strike ends in hunger. On your wall someone writes: *UMBER'S SPY*.

Il direttore della Bank è un uomo rosa e.easy: The manager of the Bank is a pink, round man who speaks softly, as if in church. He explains, very embarrassed, that your grandfather's account has never been closed. The will leaves it to Mr. Umber, and the notary has never given permission to close it. So the account is still alive: every week someone draws money with a cheque, and every month someone pays in cash, always the same amount.
Il direttore della Bank è un uomo rosa e.short: Your grandfather's account is still open, in Mr. Umber's name. Every week someone draws, every month someone pays in.

Tra gli assegni del mese scorso ce n'è u.easy: Among last month's cheques the manager shows you one separately, holding it with two fingers. The signature is one of your parents', and it is genuine. It is dated 1877. But it was written last week.
Tra gli assegni del mese scorso ce n'è u.short: One cheque bears a parent's genuine signature, dated 1877. It was written last week.

Il direttore sfoglia il registro, si bag.easy: The manager leafs through the ledger, licks his finger, leafs again. The deposits are brought by a young clerk with oversleeves, always the same one. He leaves no name and asks for no receipt. The manager knows him by sight: he is the clerk from the **Pell, Notary**. The deposits began before old Silas died. And they went on afterwards.
Il direttore sfoglia il registro, si bag.short: The deposits are brought by the clerk from the **Pell, Notary**. They began before Silas died, and go on.

Il direttore allarga le braccia. Senza i.easy: The manager spreads his hands. Without the notary's permission he can do nothing, and Ezra Pell the notary has already said no: "The account will stay open until Mr. Umber comes to close it himself." Meanwhile the rumour goes round town that the family at the estate wants Umber's money.
Il direttore allarga le braccia. Senza i.short: Ezra Pell the notary refuses: the account stays open until Umber closes it himself. And the town says you want his money.

Un biglietto piegato in quattro, infilat.easy: There is a note folded in four, pushed under your bedroom door. You know the paper: it is from your writing desk. You know the handwriting: it is yours. *Tonight, at the market. You already know.*
Un biglietto piegato in quattro, infilat.short: A note under your door, on your paper, in your hand: *Tonight, at the market. You already know.*

Un biglietto piegato in quattro, infilat.easy: There is a note folded in four, pushed under your bedroom door. The paper is the estate's. The handwriting is small, quick, and slants backwards. *See who goes to the market.*
Un biglietto piegato in quattro, infilat.short: A note under your door, slanting backwards: *See who goes to the market.*

La carta si accartoccia e diventa cenere.easy: The paper curls up and turns to ash in a moment. What is left is the smell, and the sentence, which you keep repeating to yourself until dawn.
La carta si accartoccia e diventa cenere.short: It turns to ash. The words stay in your head until dawn.

Lo infili tra le pagine del Journal, dov.easy: You put it between the pages of the Journal, where no one will look for it. Every so often, at night, you read it again. Each time the handwriting looks a little more familiar.
Lo infili tra le pagine del Journal, dov.short: You hide it in the Journal. Each time you reread it, the handwriting looks more familiar.

Quell'autunno una nebbia gialla scende d.easy: That autumn a yellow fog comes down from the hill and settles on the town like a lid. It smells of sulphur and river. The lamps are lit at noon, but it is not enough to see across the street. Carriages go at walking pace, with a boy in front waving a lantern.
Quell'autunno una nebbia gialla scende d.short: That autumn a yellow fog covers the town. The lamps are lit at noon, and it is not enough.

Nella nebbia, dicono, Umber cammina più.easy: They say Umber walks more easily in the fog. Ada Haskett's constables have orders to stop every short man in a black coat. In a week they stop forty, and let them all go.
Nella nebbia, dicono, Umber cammina più.short: Ada's constables stop every short man in a black coat: forty in a week, all released.

La quarantunesima persona fermata è **{0.easy: The forty-first person stopped is **{0}**: at two in the morning, on the bridge, with no hat, wet shoes and no explanation that convinces the constables. They spend the night in a cell at the Jail. At dawn the family can pay bail. Or it can leave them to answer Ada Haskett's questions until she is satisfied.
La quarantunesima persona fermata è **{0.short: The forty-first is **{0}**, stopped on the bridge at night. At dawn you can pay bail, or leave them to answer Ada Haskett.

La cauzione è alta, e la Gazzetta ne pub.easy: The bail is high, and the Gazette prints the exact amount. **{0}** comes home for breakfast, with a cold and no wish at all to talk about it.
La cauzione è alta, e la Gazzetta ne pub.short: You pay. **{0}** comes home with a cold, and the Gazette prints the amount.

**{0}** risponde a tutte le domande di A.easy: **{0}** answers all of Ada Haskett's questions for a whole day, patiently, and in the end walks out with no charges. Ada sees {1} to the door. "I still don't know if you told me the truth," she says. "But at least you didn't run away."
**{0}** risponde a tutte le domande di A.short: **{0}** answers Ada for a day and walks out uncharged. Ada sees {1} to the door: "At least you didn't run."

**LA CITTÀ CHE CRESCE.** Con l'apertura.easy: **THE GROWING TOWN.** With the new railway line, this year the town has passed ten thousand inhabitants. Two hundred more gas lamps have been lit, and the town council has decided to cover another stretch of the river, "for reasons of hygiene and decency".
**LA CITTÀ CHE CRESCE.** Con l'apertura.short: **THE GROWING TOWN.** With the railway the town passes ten thousand souls, and covers more of the river.

Le elezioni comunali si sono svolte rego.easy: The council elections went off normally, despite one strange candidacy: a certain *U. Mber*, whose posters covered the walls of the town hall. The candidate did not appear at the count.
Le elezioni comunali si sono svolte rego.short: A certain *U. Mber* stood in the election. He did not appear at the count.

Si è chiuso lo sciopero dei ferrovieri..easy: The railway strike is over. The union and the company tell it in opposite ways, but both speak of cheques from who knows where.
Si è chiuso lo sciopero dei ferrovieri..short: The strike is over. Everyone speaks of mysterious cheques.

L'Ispettore Ada Haskett, nipote della ce.easy: Inspector Ada Haskett, niece of the famous Nell, told this newspaper that the Umber file is "the most important thing" in her office. She added that she can count on the help of some families in the town. She did not say which.
L'Ispettore Ada Haskett, nipote della ce.short: Ada Haskett says Umber is her priority, and that some families help her. She does not say which.

Negli ambienti della Bank si parla di un.easy: At the Bank there is talk of a very old account, in a dead man's name and never closed, where a great deal of money is still moving. The manager declined to comment.
Negli ambienti della Bank si parla di un.short: At the Bank, a dead man's old account is still active. The manager declines to comment.

Nei quartieri bassi, intanto, cresce il.easy: In the poor districts, meanwhile, people are more and more angry with the family at the estate. Last night someone wrote on the boundary wall, in charcoal, a word this newspaper cannot print.
Nei quartieri bassi, intanto, cresce il.short: In the poor districts anger at the estate grows. On the wall, an unprintable word.

Per il resto, la stagione è stata tranqu.easy: Otherwise, the season has been quiet. The theatre has been full every night, the band played in the park every Sunday, and the fog, for now, has stayed on the hill.
Per il resto, la stagione è stata tranqu.short: Otherwise, a quiet season. The fog, for now, stays on the hill.

Lady Carew, con i capelli bianchi e la v.easy: Lady Carew, with white hair and the same voice as ever, is giving a party for the asylum's new wing. The whole town is invited, the family at the estate too. In fact, above all the family at the estate.
Lady Carew, con i capelli bianchi e la v.short: Lady Carew gives a party for the new wing. Everyone is invited, above all you.

Il salone del municipio è pieno di fiori.easy: The town hall's great room is full of flowers, candles and respectable people. Lady Carew greets the guests at the entrance, seated, with the leather notebook on her knees, as she did thirty years ago.
Il salone del municipio è pieno di fiori.short: Lady Carew greets the guests with her notebook on her knees, as thirty years ago.

Quando ti vede ti tende la mano e ti ric.easy: When she sees you she gives you her hand and reminds you, smiling, that your family's name is still on the brass plaque at the asylum entrance. "Generous families," she says, "are not forgotten."
Quando ti vede ti tende la mano e ti ric.short: She gives you her hand: your name is still on the asylum plaque. "Generous families are not forgotten."

Quando ti vede non ti tende la mano. \"A.easy: When she sees you she does not give you her hand. "Ah," she says, loud enough for everyone to hear. "The family with no need of asylums." Someone laughs. You do not.
Quando ti vede non ti tende la mano. \"A.short: She does not give you her hand: "Ah, the family with no need of asylums." Someone laughs. You do not.

Quando ti vede ti saluta con un cenno, c.easy: When she sees you she greets you with a nod, the way one greets a family one knows everything about, and points you to the buffet.
Quando ti vede ti saluta con un cenno, c.short: She nods, like someone who knows all about you, and points you to the buffet.

Lady Carew smette di sorridere. Si guard.easy: Lady Carew stops smiling. She looks around, closes the notebook and signals you to come closer. "Not here," she whispers. "Tomorrow, after the party, come to me. I shall tell you everything. And in return you will tell me one thing only: a name." Half the room saw you talking quietly, and the other half will hear about it.
Lady Carew smette di sorridere. Si guard.short: "Not here," Lady Carew whispers. "Tomorrow I shall tell you everything. In return I want a name." Half the room saw you.

Balli il valzer con la moglie del sindac.easy: You waltz with the mayor's wife, drink the asylum's champagne and tell jokes to the bank manager. For one evening the family at the estate is a family like any other, and everyone seems glad to believe it.
Balli il valzer con la moglie del sindac.short: You dance, drink, joke. For one evening you are a family like any other, and everyone is glad to believe it.

Quando Lady Carew si alza per il discors.easy: When Lady Carew stands up for her speech, the notebook stays on the armchair. You slip it under your jacket and leave by the service door. At home you read it all: names, illnesses, *interesting cases*, and the accounts of the gentlefolk's ward, paid for years by Umber. The last line, in Lady Carew's small hand, is from this morning: *Tomorrow. The name.*
Quando Lady Carew si alza per il discors.short: You steal Lady Carew's notebook. Inside, the accounts Umber paid. The last line, from this morning: *Tomorrow. The name.*

Il becchino del cimitero nuovo è un uomo.easy: The gravedigger at the new cemetery is a cheerful man who whistles as he digs. He is preparing a grave in a quiet corner, by the wall, under a lime tree. He explains that it is for a client who is not dead yet. He paid for everything in advance: the grave, the headstone and even the flowers, which must be violets. With a cheque.
Il becchino del cimitero nuovo è un uomo.short: The gravedigger is digging for a client not yet dead, who has paid for everything, violets included. With a cheque.

Il becchino tira fuori dal panciotto un.easy: The gravedigger takes a crumpled sheet from his waistcoat. The order is signed *Umber*, in the usual hand. Where the headstone's words should be, it says only *Here lies the one who kept the key*. The space for the date is empty. "Folk who plan ahead," says the gravedigger, and goes back to digging.
Il becchino tira fuori dal panciotto un.short: The order is signed *Umber*. For the headstone: *Here lies the one who kept the key*. No date.

Il becchino ride di cuore, poi si accorg.easy: The gravedigger laughs heartily, then realises you are not joking. He shows you a free spot in the sun, away from the wall, and gives you a good price. You sign the order in your own upright hand, and feel strangely relieved: at least this, in your life, will be in its proper place.
Il becchino ride di cuore, poi si accorg.short: You buy a grave in the sun and sign in your upright hand. At least this will be in its place.

L'architetto del nuovo padiglione del ma.easy: The architect of the asylum's new wing has hung his drawings on the walls of the Builder's Office, like paintings. He proudly shows you everything: the bright corridors, the single rooms, the winter garden. In the farthest corner, where the wing touches the alley, there is a small service door that is not in the official drawings.
L'architetto del nuovo padiglione del ma.short: The new wing's plans show a small door onto the alley that is missing from the official ones.

L'architetto arrossisce. \"Lady Carew in.easy: The architect goes red. "Lady Carew herself," he says. "A private door, for discreet visits. Only she has the key." Then he lowers his voice: "And a gentleman who visits her late in the evening. A benefactor. Short in stature."
L'architetto arrossisce. \"Lady Carew in.short: "Lady Carew wanted it, for discreet visits. And for a benefactor who comes late at night. Short in stature."

L'architetto ti fa copiare i disegni da.easy: The architect has an apprentice copy the drawings and signs them, so they are genuine. At home you study them all night. The wing is well built. It has only one weak point, and that is the little door onto the alley.
L'architetto ti fa copiare i disegni da.short: You get copies of the plans. The wing has one weak point: the little door onto the alley.

Sul tendone della compagnia c'è un manif.easy: On the company's tent there is a hand-painted poster: *THE DOCTOR AND HIS DOUBLE – a drama in three acts, from a true story.* The doctor is tall and elegant, and drinks a white salt from a smoking glass. The double is small, wears a black coat that is too big, and laughs.
Sul tendone della compagnia c'è un manif.short: The players are giving *THE DOCTOR AND HIS DOUBLE*, "from a true story". The double is small, in a black coat, and laughs.

Il pubblico ride con lui. Ogni tanto, ne.easy: The audience laughs with him. Every now and then, in the dark, someone turns to look at you.
Il pubblico ride con lui. Ogni tanto, ne.short: The audience laughs. Now and then someone turns to look at you.

Il capocomico prende il denaro con un in.easy: The manager takes the money with a bow, and the next morning the tent is gone. But the posters stay on the walls for months, faded by the rain, and the little painted man goes on laughing from every corner.
Il capocomico prende il denaro con un in.short: You pay, and the company leaves. But the little man on the posters still laughs from every wall.

Nel terzo atto il dottore insegue il dop.easy: In the third act the doctor chases the double across the rooftops, catches him and pulls off his hat: underneath is his son's face. Applause. At the bows there are six actors, but the programme listed five. The one who played the double is not in the programme. And when you look for his dressing room behind the tent, you cannot find it.
Nel terzo atto il dottore insegue il dop.short: In the end the double has the doctor's son's face. At the bows there are six actors; the programme lists five. The sixth is gone.

Sali sul palco a metà del secondo atto,.easy: Halfway through the second act you climb onto the stage, stand among the actors and tell the audience it is all true. The audience applauds, thinking it is improvisation. After the show, the manager offers you a permanent part.
Sali sul palco a metà del secondo atto,.short: You climb on stage and say it is all true. The audience applauds, and the manager offers you a part.

Nella biblioteca nuova, sullo scaffale d.easy: In the new library, on the natural sciences shelf, is the only book the old man ever published: *An Essay on the Dual Nature of Man*, 1858. It is very worn. The margins are full of pencil notes, in small handwriting that slants backwards: corrections, calculations, exclamation marks.
Nella biblioteca nuova, sullo scaffale d.short: The library holds the old man's book, *An Essay on the Dual Nature of Man*. Its margins are full of notes, slanting backwards.

Sulla scheda dei prestiti, incollata in.easy: On the lending card glued in the back of the book there is always the same name, every month, for twenty years: *Pell, Notary*. The latest dates are after Silas's death.
Sulla scheda dei prestiti, incollata in.short: For twenty years the *Pell, Notary* has borrowed it, even after Silas died.

Lo porti alla tenuta e lo leggi in una n.easy: You take it to the estate and read it in one night. The essay is dull, arrogant and brilliant, like its author. The notes in the margins are better than the essay. Someone, all these years, has carried on the old man's work. The next day the library comes looking for you: the book was reserved.
Lo porti alla tenuta e lo leggi in una n.short: You read it in one night. The notes beat the essay: someone has carried on the old man's work.

Rimetti il libro al suo posto, con il do.easy: You put the book back in its place, lined up with the others. When you come back a week later, it is gone. The librarian says the usual gentleman from the notary's office took it. She finds it odd that you care.
Rimetti il libro al suo posto, con il do.short: You leave it. A week later the usual gentleman from the notary's office has taken it.

**ORRIBILE DELITTO DIETRO IL MANICOMIO.*.easy: **HORRIBLE MURDER BEHIND THE ASYLUM.** Lady Carew, benefactor of the town and founder of the asylum on the hill, was found dead at dawn in the alley beside the new wing. It seems she had stepped out for some air after the party. She was struck many times with a walking stick, with a fury the police surgeon called "inhuman".
**ORRIBILE DELITTO DIETRO IL MANICOMIO.*.short: **HORRIBLE MURDER BEHIND THE ASYLUM.** Lady Carew was beaten to death at dawn in the alley with a walking stick, with "inhuman" fury.

Una cameriera, affacciata a una finestra.easy: A maid at a top-floor window saw the attacker in the fog: a small man in a black coat that was too big, who walked away afterwards without hurrying, whistling. Near the body the police found half of the stick, broken. On the silver handle are the initials of the family at the estate.
Una cameriera, affacciata a una finestra.short: A maid saw a small man in a black coat stroll off whistling. The broken stick bears your family's initials.

La città vuole un colpevole. L'Ispettore.easy: The town wants someone to blame. Inspector Ada Haskett has promised to find them before Christmas.
La città vuole un colpevole. L'Ispettore.short: The town wants someone to blame by Christmas.

Lady Carew aveva promesso a uno di voi d.easy: Lady Carew had promised to tell one of you everything, the day after the party. She did not live to do it. Half the room saw you talking quietly with her, and Ada Haskett knows it.
Lady Carew aveva promesso a uno di voi d.short: Lady Carew was to tell you everything the day after the party. She did not live to, and Ada knows you spoke.

In famiglia qualcuno ricorda il libretto.easy: Someone in the family remembers Lady Carew's leather notebook, and the page with the accounts of the gentlefolk's ward: a cheque every month, for years, signed *Umber*. Whoever pays for so long sooner or later stops paying. Or starts asking for something in return.
In famiglia qualcuno ricorda il libretto.short: Umber paid Lady Carew for years. Whoever pays that long stops sooner or later. Or asks for something back.

Il funerale di Lady Carew è il più grand.easy: Lady Carew's funeral is the biggest the town has ever seen: the bishop, the mayor, all the asylum doctors in a line, and behind them half the town in black. The procession passes the estate gate. The family must decide: join the procession, or stay indoors with the curtains drawn.
Il funerale di Lady Carew è il più grand.short: Lady Carew's funeral passes the estate. Do you join the procession, or stay in with the curtains drawn?

Il vescovo vi accoglie con una stretta d.easy: The bishop greets you with a handshake: your family's name is on the asylum's brass plaque, and everyone knows it. During the sermon some people give you dark looks, but no one dares say anything.
Il vescovo vi accoglie con una stretta d.short: The bishop shakes your hand: you are on the asylum plaque. Some glare, but say nothing.

Vi fate largo fino alla prima fila. La f.easy: You push your way to the front row. The crowd murmurs. A woman says, loud enough for everyone to hear, that the murderer always returns to the scene of the crime, or at least to the funeral.
Vi fate largo fino alla prima fila. La f.short: You go to the front row. A woman says aloud that the murderer always comes to the funeral.

La corona è la più grande del corteo, bi.easy: Your wreath is the biggest in the procession, white and violet, with a ribbon and the family's name in gold letters. The Gazette describes it admiringly. It cost a good deal.
La corona è la più grande del corteo, bi.short: Your wreath is the biggest, and the Gazette admires it. It cost a good deal.

Restate a casa, con le tende tirate, men.easy: You stay indoors, curtains drawn, while the procession passes the gate. From the street someone throws a stone at a ground-floor window. The glass breaks. None of you goes down to pick up the pieces.
Restate a casa, con le tende tirate, men.short: You stay in. Someone throws a stone through a window. No one goes down.

Lady Carew è morta da tre mesi e non ho.easy: Lady Carew has been dead three months and I have nothing. I have a broken stick with a family's initials, a maid who saw a small man in the fog, and a town that wants someone to blame by Christmas. My aunt says there is always someone to blame. The trouble is that usually there is more than one.
Lady Carew è morta da tre mesi e non ho.short: Three months and no proof: a stick, a maid, an impatient town. My aunt says there is usually more than one to blame.

Mezzo salone, la sera della festa, ha vi.easy: On the night of the party half the room saw Lady Carew talking quietly with someone from the estate. She had promised to give them a name, the next day. She died first. I do not know if that person is a witness or an accomplice. I know they are afraid.
Mezzo salone, la sera della festa, ha vi.short: Lady Carew was to give someone from the estate a name. I do not know if they are a witness or an accomplice. I know they are afraid.

Il libretto rilegato in pelle di Lady Ca.easy: Lady Carew's leather notebook, the one she always carried, was not on the body and not in her house. Someone took it. I have an idea who.
Il libretto rilegato in pelle di Lady Ca.short: Lady Carew's notebook is gone. I have an idea who took it.

In città si parla ancora del *Dottore e.easy: The town still talks about *The Doctor and His Double*, the travelling players' show, and some people go looking for Lady Carew's murderer among the actors, as if going to the circus. I asked the manager who played the double. He does not know. He never knew.
In città si parla ancora del *Dottore e.short: I asked the manager who played the double. He never knew.

Uno degli eredi ha preso in prestito il.easy: One of the heirs borrowed the old man's book from the library, the one the Pell office reserves every month. The next day the notary's clerk came to ask for it back, so insistently that it struck me as odd. I made a note.
Uno degli eredi ha preso in prestito il.short: An heir borrowed the old man's book, and Pell's clerk demanded it back. I made a note.

Il becchino del cimitero nuovo dice di a.easy: The gravedigger at the new cemetery says that months ago he got an order for a grave for someone still alive, paid with a cheque from Umber, with no date. I asked him not to fill it in. He laughed.
Il becchino del cimitero nuovo dice di a.short: Umber paid for a grave for someone living, undated. I asked the gravedigger not to fill it in. He laughed.

Domani ricomincio da capo, dalla tenuta..easy: Tomorrow I start again from the beginning, at the estate. My aunt says that is always where it ends.
Domani ricomincio da capo, dalla tenuta..short: Tomorrow I start again at the estate. My aunt says it always ends there.

Natale è passato da un pezzo, e il colpe.easy: Christmas is long past, and there is no one to blame. Ada Haskett has stopped searching the streets: now she is searching the estate.
Natale è passato da un pezzo, e il colpe.short: Christmas has passed, and Ada Haskett now looks for the culprit at the estate.

Alla Bank ti aspetta una lettera, lascia.easy: At the Bank there is a letter for you, left at the counter by a boy who ran straight off. Inside, letters of every size cut from newspapers make up a single sentence: *I KNOW WHICH OF YOU GOES OUT AT NIGHT. LEAVE THE MONEY IN SAFE DEPOSIT BOX 14, OR THE INSPECTOR WILL KNOW TOO.* The cashier says box 14 belongs to the Pell's notary practice, but the office has not used it for years.
Alla Bank ti aspetta una lettera, lascia.short: An anonymous letter: *I KNOW WHICH OF YOU GOES OUT AT NIGHT. LEAVE THE MONEY IN SAFE DEPOSIT BOX 14, OR THE INSPECTOR WILL KNOW TOO.* The box is the Pell office's.

Lasci il denaro nella cassetta 14, in un.easy: You leave the money in box 14, in an unmarked envelope. A week later you go back to check. The envelope is gone, and in its place is a handwritten note, in the backward-slanting hand: *Thank you. I shall bear it in mind.*
Lasci il denaro nella cassetta 14, in un.short: You pay. A week later, in the box, a note slanting backwards: *Thank you. I shall bear it in mind.*

Ada legge la lettera, la gira, la annusa.easy: Ada reads the letter, turns it over, sniffs it and seals it in a police envelope. She has box 14 opened with a warrant. Inside there is only dust, and an old empty pen case. "Someone knew you would come to me," she says. "Or hoped you wouldn't."
Ada legge la lettera, la gira, la annusa.short: Ada has the box opened: just dust and an empty pen case. "Someone knew you would come to me. Or hoped not."

La strappi in otto pezzi e la butti nel.easy: You tear it into eight pieces and drop it in the bank's wastepaper basket. Two days later, in the Gazette's gossip column, there is a rhyming riddle about a family "that goes out by night and tears up its post by day". The town laughs for a week.
La strappi in otto pezzi e la butti nel.short: You tear it up. Two days later the Gazette prints a riddle about a family "that goes out by night and tears up its post by day".

Il caposquadra della fonderia è un omone.easy: The foundry foreman is a huge man with burn-scarred arms and a memory like an archive. When you describe the silver handle of the stick found near Lady Carew, he nods at once. "We cast it," he says. "Forty years ago, for the old man at the estate. One of a kind. The old man always carried that stick."
Il caposquadra della fonderia è un omone.short: The foreman knows the stick's handle: "We cast it, for the old man at the estate. He always carried it."

Il caposquadra ci pensa a lungo. Poi acc.easy: The foreman thinks for a long time. Then he agrees, for a small fee and for the love of truth, in that order. Before Inspector Haskett he will swear that the stick belonged to the old man, gone for nearly thirty years, and that no one in the family has seen it since.
Il caposquadra ci pensa a lungo. Poi acc.short: For a small fee he will swear to the Inspector that the stick was the old man's, and none of you has seen it since.

\"Una copia no\", dice il caposquadra. \.easy: "No copy," says the foreman. "But three years ago a gentleman came to have the handle polished. With the whole stick. A small gentleman, in a black coat too big for him. He paid with a cheque." He laughs. "And the cheque was good."
\"Una copia no\", dice il caposquadra. \.short: "Three years ago a small gentleman in a black coat had it polished. He paid by cheque. And it was good."

Sulla tomba di Silas Pell c'è una lapide.easy: On Silas Pell's grave there is a new headstone of white marble, too big for a man who did not like to be noticed. In front of it stands his son, Ezra Pell the notary: thin, dressed in black, with the eyes of someone who sleeps little. He greets you with a bow, the way one greets a client. He is your family's notary now, and he has read the whole file.
Sulla tomba di Silas Pell c'è una lapide.short: At Silas's grave stands his son, Ezra Pell, thin and tired. He is your notary now, and has read the file.

Poi, dopo un momento: \"Negli ultimi ann.easy: Then, after a moment: "In his last years, though, he was afraid of you. Of one of you, at least. He never told me why."
Poi, dopo un momento: \"Negli ultimi ann.short: "In his last years he was afraid of one of you. He never told me why."

Ezra ascolta senza interromperti, con un.easy: Ezra listens without interrupting, with a strange, almost hungry attention. He asks you the colour of the salt in the glass, how many sips, how many hours it lasts. In the end he thanks you, shakes your hand and offers to keep the family's papers in his office, "safe, under lock and key". His fingers are cold.
Ezra ascolta senza interromperti, con un.short: Ezra listens hungrily: colour, sips, hours. Then he offers to keep your papers "under lock and key". His fingers are cold.

Ezra ride, una risata breve e nervosa. \.easy: Ezra laughs, a short, nervous laugh. "The cupboard! I have never found the key. I called in two locksmiths, and neither could open it. My father kept his powders there, when he was young and wanted to be an apothecary." He touches his waistcoat, where his father kept the little packet. "If I open it, you will be the first to know."
Ezra ride, una risata breve e nervosa. \.short: "The cupboard? I never found the key. My father kept his powders there." He touches his waistcoat. "If I open it, you will be the first to know."

Lasci sulla lapide un mazzetto di violet.easy: You leave a little bunch of violets on the headstone. Ezra looks at it and turns pale. "Violets," he says. "Someone used to bring them to your grandfather too, every morning. My father told me." Then he recovers, thanks you and walks you to the gate.
Lasci sulla lapide un mazzetto di violet.short: You leave violets. Ezra turns pale: "Someone used to bring them to your grandfather every morning."

Lomax è invecchiato, ormai. Ha chiuso la.easy: Lomax is old now. He has closed his pharmacy and sells his salts from a counter at the back of the General Store, among the brooms and oil lamps. His fingers are still stained yellow, and he still looks like a man waiting for bad news. The difference is that now he seems to know which.
Lomax è invecchiato, ormai. Ha chiuso la.short: Old Lomax sells his salts at the back of the General Store. He seems to await bad news, and to know which.

Ti riconosce subito: sei della famiglia.easy: He recognises you at once: you are from the family that grabbed him by the collar at the market, years ago. He will not speak to you.
Ti riconosce subito: sei della famiglia.short: He knows you: the family from the market. He will not speak to you.

Ti riconosce subito. \"Avete ancora la m.easy: He recognises you at once. "Do you still have my page?" he asks quietly. "Keep it safe. One day you will need it."
Ti riconosce subito. \"Avete ancora la m.short: "Do you still have my page? Keep it safe. One day you will need it."

Lomax te la incarta con le mani che trem.easy: Lomax wraps it for you with shaking hands. "It's the best," he says. "It's pure. And that's the trouble." That evening, in the glass, the colour stops at the first red, as always.
Lomax te la incarta con le mani che trem.short: "It's the best. It's pure. And that's the trouble." In the glass it stops at red, as always.

Lomax chiama il padrone del negozio con.easy: Lomax calls the shopkeeper in a faint voice. The shopkeeper shows you to the door, politely, in front of all the customers. On the pavement a lady recognises you and crosses herself.
Lomax chiama il padrone del negozio con.short: Lomax calls the shopkeeper, who shows you out. Outside, a lady crosses herself.

Lomax si guarda intorno, poi si china ve.easy: Lomax looks around, then leans towards you. His breath smells of mint and fear. "Grey," he whispers. "The powder was grey. A teaspoon per phial. Don't ask me whose it was." Then he goes back to counting his boxes, and says nothing more.
Lomax si guarda intorno, poi si china ve.short: "Grey," Lomax whispers. "The powder was grey. A teaspoon per phial. Don't ask me whose it was."

La chiesa è piena di gente che non vuole.easy: The church is full of people who do not want to sleep at home: whole families on the pews, with blankets and lanterns, praying softly. The confessional is at the back, in the dark. You kneel. Behind the grille a tired voice says: "Go on."
La chiesa è piena di gente che non vuole.short: The church is full of people afraid to sleep at home. In the confessional, a tired voice: "Go on."

Racconti tutto, anche quello che non ric.easy: You tell everything, even what you do not remember. The priest is silent for a long time. Then, very quietly: "The other one came here too, last night. He confessed the same things, in the same order. With your voice." When you leave the confessional, the other side of the grille is empty.
Racconti tutto, anche quello che non ric.short: You tell everything. The priest whispers: "The other one came last night. He confessed the same things. With your voice."

Confessi un peccato inventato, piccolo e.easy: You confess an invented sin, small and believable, to see what happens. "Liar," says the voice behind the grille, and laughs. It is not the priest's voice. When you open the curtain, the priest is only now coming from the sacristy, stole in hand, apologising for being late.
Confessi un peccato inventato, piccolo e.short: You confess a made-up sin. "Liar," the voice laughs. But the priest is only now arriving from the sacristy.

Non dici niente. Dall'altra parte della.easy: You say nothing. On the other side of the grille someone breathes slowly, for a long time, then gets up and leaves. On the confessional step you find a cheque folded in four, payable to bearer, in the backward-slanting hand. It is alms. For you.
Non dici niente. Dall'altra parte della.short: You stay silent. Someone breathes behind the grille, then leaves. On the step, a backward-slanting cheque: alms for you.

L'Ispettore Ada Haskett si presenta alla.easy: One winter evening Inspector Ada Haskett comes to the estate, alone, with the broken stick wrapped in a handkerchief. She sits down in the library without taking off her coat and lays it on the table, between you.
L'Ispettore Ada Haskett si presenta alla.short: One evening Ada Haskett comes alone and lays the broken stick on the table between you.

\"Non credo ai fantasmi\", dice, \"e nem.easy: "I don't believe in ghosts," she says, "nor in men who don't grow old. I believe in initials on handles and in muddy shoes. Umber is in this room. Either you tell me, or I choose."
\"Non credo ai fantasmi\", dice, \"e nem.short: "I don't believe in ghosts. I believe in initials and mud. Umber is in this room. You tell me, or I choose."

Sul tavolo, accanto al bastone, c'è anch.easy: On the table, beside the stick, is the foundry foreman's statement too: the stick was the old man's, and no one in the family had seen it for nearly thirty years. Ada touches it with one finger, as if to see whether it is hot.
Sul tavolo, accanto al bastone, c'è anch.short: Beside it lies the foreman's statement: the stick was the old man's. Ada touches it as if it burned.

Poi aggiunge, più piano: \"Mi avete aiut.easy: Then she adds, more quietly: "You helped me, and I don't forget it. If you get it wrong, I won't be the one who makes you pay."
Poi aggiunge, più piano: \"Mi avete aiut.short: "You helped me. If you get it wrong, I won't make you pay."

Poi apre il fascicolo e posa sul tavolo,.easy: Then she opens the file and puts on the table, in plain view, the coins you gave her. "These," she says, "are already on record."
Poi apre il fascicolo e posa sul tavolo,.short: Then she lays your coins on the table. "These are already on record."

Ada Haskett conta il denaro due volte, l.easy: Ada Haskett counts the money twice, puts it in an envelope and writes on it: *for police widows*. Then she closes the file, stands and leaves without saying goodbye. The next day the Gazette reports that Lady Carew's murderer was a tramp, drowned in the river.
Ada Haskett conta il denaro due volte, l.short: Ada puts the money in an envelope *for police widows* and leaves. The Gazette says the murderer was a drowned tramp.

In città nessuno ci crede. Si dice che l.easy: No one in town believes it. They say the family at the estate bought the police's silence. And people, when they cannot have someone to blame, are happy to settle for a suspicion.
In città nessuno ci crede. Si dice che l.short: No one believes it. They say you bought the police, and a suspicion is enough.

Le guardie perquisiscono la camera dell'.easy: The constables search the accused's room. In the wardrobe they find shoes caked with river mud. In the pocket of a black coat that is too tight they find a bundle of signed cheques. Under the mattress is the other half of the stick. The handwriting on the cheques slants backwards.
Le guardie perquisiscono la camera dell'.short: In the accused's room they find muddy shoes, backward-slanting cheques and the other half of the stick.

Al processo l'accusato giura di non rico.easy: At the trial the accused swears they remember nothing, and everyone in court laughs. Everyone except Ada Haskett, who looks at them for a long time, the way one looks at someone telling the truth. That night, for the first time in thirty years, no one sees Umber in town.
Al processo l'accusato giura di non rico.short: At the trial the accused remembers nothing. All laugh but Ada. That night, for the first time in thirty years, no one sees Umber.

Le guardie perquisiscono la camera dell'.easy: The constables search the accused's room and find nothing: no muddy shoes, no cheques, no half of the stick. Ada Haskett takes them away anyway, because the town wants it. But the next morning she lets them go for lack of evidence, and tells the Gazette the investigation continues.
Le guardie perquisiscono la camera dell'.short: The accused's room holds nothing. Ada takes them in, but frees them next morning: the investigation goes on.

Quella notte, mentre la famiglia festegg.easy: That night, while the family celebrates the homecoming, someone laughs at the end of the alley.
Quella notte, mentre la famiglia festegg.short: That night you celebrate. At the end of the alley, someone laughs.

Le guardie perquisiscono la camera dell'.easy: The constables search the accused's room and find nothing: no muddy shoes, no cheques, no half of the stick. They take them away anyway, because the town wants someone to blame and Christmas is long past. The Jail has a free cell, with a window onto the alley.
Le guardie perquisiscono la camera dell'.short: The accused's room holds nothing, but they take them anyway. Their cell looks onto the alley.

Quella notte, mentre l'accusato guarda l.easy: That night, while the prisoner watches the stars between the bars, someone laughs at the end of the alley.
Quella notte, mentre l'accusato guarda l.short: That night, at the end of the alley, someone laughs.

Le sei boccette del vecchio sono vuote:.easy: The old man's six phials are empty: someone in the family drank or threw away the last grain, and no one admits it. They are still in the zinc box, under the loose board by the stove, with broken sealing wax and faded labels: *Lomax's Pharmacy – first batch*. On the glass at the bottom there is a greyish film that will not come off, even with boiling water.
Le sei boccette del vecchio sono vuote:.short: The six phials are empty, and no one admits emptying them. A grey film clings to the bottom.

Le rimettete nella cassetta di zinco, e.easy: You put them back in the zinc box, and the box back under the board. No one knows what empty phials could be good for. But no one has the heart to throw them away.
Le rimettete nella cassetta di zinco, e.short: You put them back. They are useless, but no one can throw them away.

Ezra Pell le riceve nel suo studio, le e.easy: Ezra Pell receives them in his office, studies them one by one against the light of the window and locks them in a glass cabinet, with a care that moves you. "They will be safe," he says. "Safer than with you."
Ezra Pell le riceve nel suo studio, le e.short: You give them to Ezra Pell, who locks them away with great care. "Safer than with you."

Le buttate dal ponte, una alla volta, in.easy: You throw them off the bridge, one at a time, on a moonless night. The river swallows them without a sound. A week later a fisherman pulls one out and sells it to the junk dealer as a souvenir of the old man at the estate.
Le buttate dal ponte, una alla volta, in.short: You throw them in the river. A fisherman fishes one out and sells it to the junk dealer.

Il farmacista Lomax, ormai vecchio, vend.easy: Lomax the chemist, now old, still sells the salt: white, fine, with a new label and the old price. But in the glass the colour no longer changes as it used to. It turns red and stops there. When people ask him why, old Lomax looks at the floor and says today's salt is too pure.
Il farmacista Lomax, ormai vecchio, vend.short: Lomax still sells the salt. But in the glass it stops at red: "Today's salt is too pure."

Nell'inverno del 1895 morì, in una camer.easy: In the winter of 1895, in a rented room near the river, an old man with no papers died: small, thin, in a black coat too big for him. They buried him in the common grave. I was the only one at the funeral. I had read the file, and I knew who he was.
Nell'inverno del 1895 morì, in una camer.short: In the winter of 1895 a nameless old man died by the river, small, in a black coat. I alone was at the funeral. I knew who he was.

Quello stesso inverno, frugando tra le c.easy: That same winter, going through my father's papers, I finally found the key to the cupboard: it was sewn into the lining of his coat. I shall not write here what I found inside. I write only that since then I sleep little, and that the cupboard is now empty.
Quello stesso inverno, frugando tra le c.short: That winter I found the cupboard key, sewn into my father's coat. I shall not write what was inside. The cupboard is empty now.

Non lo dissi alla famiglia della tenuta,.easy: I did not tell the family at the estate, though I had promised they would be the first to know. They had trusted me. It was the worst mistake of their lives, and the most useful of mine.
Non lo dissi alla famiglia della tenuta,.short: I did not tell the family, who trusted me. It was their worst mistake, and my most useful.

La città ha la luce elettrica, il tram e.easy: The town has electric light, trams and two newspapers that hate each other. One is liberal and blames everything on the rich. The other is conservative and blames everything on the poor. On one thing they agree: Mr. Umber sells copies. On the hill, near the asylum, a new Institute of Science has gone up, all glass and brass. Its professors write to the papers that the estate's salt is a country superstition.
La città ha la luce elettrica, il tram e.short: The town has electric light and two papers that hate each other, but Umber sells copies of both. The new Institute's professors call the salt a superstition.

Si sbagliano, ma non del tutto. Negli an.easy: They are wrong, but not entirely. In recent years some young people in town bought the new salt from Lomax, for a bet or out of despair, and drank it. The new salt works: the other one comes out, as always. But in the morning it does not go back. Two of them are in the asylum, laughing day and night. No one has seen the third again. I knew him. He was my neighbour's son, and he always raised his hat to me.
Si sbagliano, ma non del tutto. Negli an.short: They are wrong. Three young people drank the new salt: the other came out, but never went back. Two laugh in the asylum, the third has vanished.

Io, quanto a me, ho cinquantasei anni e.easy: As for me, I am fifty-six, with a cough the doctors cannot cure. I sleep little, write badly and wear gloves even in summer, because of eczema on my hands. The practice runs by itself, with the old clerk treating me like a sick son. I have decided to keep this file in order to the end. Whoever reads it after me will judge whether it was worth it.
Io, quanto a me, ho cinquantasei anni e.short: I am fifty-six, with a cough no one can cure. I sleep little, write badly, wear gloves even in summer for eczema. I shall keep this file in order to the end.

Una busta dello studio notarile Pell, co.easy: An envelope has come from the Pell's notary practice, with your name handwritten so shakily that the postman had to ask the address twice. Inside are a few lines. The notary begs you, "for the good of the family and in the name of the friendship that has always bound our families", to bring him something from the estate in secret, without telling anyone.
Una busta dello studio notarile Pell, co.short: A letter from Pell the notary, in a shaky hand. He asks you to bring him something from the estate in secret.

*Una pagina del Journal del vecchio, una.easy: *A page of the old man's Journal, any page, as long as it is in his night-time hand.*
*Una pagina del Journal del vecchio, una.short: *A page of the Journal, in the night-time hand.*

*Un pizzico del sale nuovo che usate in.easy: *A pinch of the new salt you use in the laboratory, well wrapped in paper.*
*Un pizzico del sale nuovo che usate in.short: *A pinch of the new salt, well wrapped.*

*Una copia della chiave del vostro cance.easy: *A copy of the key to your gate, which I shall return within the week.*
*Una copia della chiave del vostro cance.short: *A copy of the gate key, for a week.*

*Un capello del vecchio, dalla spazzola.easy: *A hair of the old man's, from the silver brush that should still be on his chest of drawers.*
*Un capello del vecchio, dalla spazzola.short: *A hair of the old man's, from his silver brush.*

Lo porti allo studio il giorno dopo, in.easy: The next day you take it to the office, in an unmarked envelope. The clerk takes it without looking you in the face. Two days later a thank-you note arrives, with some money, "for your trouble".
Lo porti allo studio il giorno dopo, in.short: You take it to the office. Two days later come thanks and money, "for your trouble".

Metti la lettera in un cassetto e non ri.easy: You put the letter in a drawer and do not reply. The notary does not insist. But that shaky handwriting, who knows why, comes back to you every time you open the drawer.
Metti la lettera in un cassetto e non ri.short: You do not reply. But that shaky hand comes back to you every time you open the drawer.

Mostri la lettera agli altri, a cena, e.easy: At dinner you show the letter to the others and read it aloud. Someone laughs: the old notary is losing his mind. Someone else does not laugh at all, and wants to know whether the others have received one too.
Mostri la lettera agli altri, a cena, e.short: You read it at dinner. Someone laughs. Someone else does not, and asks if the others got one too.

A colazione nessuno parla di lettere. Il.easy: At breakfast no one mentions letters. The tram passes the gate at eight o'clock sharp, as it does every morning. The reporter from the liberal paper is already waiting across the street, notebook in hand.
A colazione nessuno parla di lettere. Il.short: At breakfast no one mentions letters. Outside, the reporter waits with his notebook.

L'Ispettore Ada Haskett, prima di andare.easy: Before retiring, Inspector Ada Haskett had all the cheques of the last twenty years examined again. The result is on the library table, in a police envelope: none of them was written by anyone in the family. None of you was Umber, and none of you ever has been.
L'Ispettore Ada Haskett, prima di andare.short: Ada Haskett's new report says none of the cheques was written by you. None of you has ever been Umber.

Eppure gli assegni continuano ad arrivar.easy: And yet the cheques keep coming, with your names. The slanting hand is always the same, the old man's. Only it is more tired and slower, like the hand of a man growing old. So who is signing them?
Eppure gli assegni continuano ad arrivar.short: Yet the cheques still come, in the old man's hand, only wearier. Who signs them?

L'Erede nell'Ombra è morto in prigione m.easy: The Heir in the Shadow died in prison many years ago, remembering nothing, and the town celebrated. But blood does not stop. No one in the family says it aloud, but everyone has noticed: when the youngest write in a hurry, their hand begins to slant backwards.
L'Erede nell'Ombra è morto in prigione m.short: The Heir in the Shadow died in prison. But when the youngest write fast, their hand slants backwards.

Una sera, a cena, chi porta il sangue de.easy: One evening at dinner, whoever carries the blood of the Heir in the Shadow puts down their knife and fork and tells everything: the nights, the muddy shoes, the cheques, the broken stick in the alley. No one interrupts. At the end someone pours everyone a drink, and dinner goes on. There is nothing left to hide: Umber is family, like the silver and the debts.
Una sera, a cena, chi porta il sangue de.short: At dinner the one with the Heir in the Shadow's blood tells all. No one interrupts. Umber is family, like the silver and the debts.

In soffitta, in un baule chiuso con lo s.easy: In the attic, in a trunk tied with string, there is a black coat. It is too wide for a small man and too short for a tall one. The pockets are worn, a horn button has been replaced with a bone one and, in the lining, there is a dark stain no one wants to sniff. No one knows who put it there. Everyone knows whose it is.
In soffitta, in un baule chiuso con lo s.short: In the attic is a black coat with a dark stain in the lining. No one knows who put it there. Everyone knows whose it is.

Il cappotto brucia male, con un fumo ner.easy: The coat burns badly, with thick black smoke that smells of tobacco and acid. From their windows the neighbours see the fire and talk about it for days: the family at the estate is burning the evidence.
Il cappotto brucia male, con un fumo ner.short: You burn it. The neighbours say you are burning the evidence.

Lo appendete all'attaccapanni dell'ingre.easy: You hang it on the hall coat stand, next to your own. Visitors notice it at once, and no one dares ask. Some mornings it seems to have moved one hook along. Some mornings its sleeves are wet.
Lo appendete all'attaccapanni dell'ingre.short: You hang it in the hall. Some mornings it has moved a hook, or its sleeves are wet.

La compagnia che recita *Il dottore e il.easy: The company performing *The Doctor and His Double* takes it gladly: it is the perfect costume. From that evening the actor who plays Umber wears it on stage, and swears he feels good in it. Too good.
La compagnia che recita *Il dottore e il.short: You give it to the players. The actor who plays Umber feels good in it. Too good.

I due giornali della città si contendono.easy: The town's two papers fight over Umber. For the liberal paper he is a rich man amusing himself at the expense of the poor. For the conservative one he is a poor man dressed up as a rich one. Both send a reporter to the estate, every morning.
I due giornali della città si contendono.short: One paper says Umber is rich, the other poor. Both send a reporter to the estate.

Il terzo esperimento riesce all'alba, do.easy: The third experiment succeeds at dawn, after a whole night of broken glass and matches. In the glass, at last, the colour changes as it used to: red, then dark violet, then pond green. Then, slowly, it turns clear as water. It is not the old man's salt: it is its opposite. Whoever drinks it becomes one person again, for ever.
Il terzo esperimento riesce all'alba, do.short: At dawn it works: red, violet, green, then clear. It is the salt's opposite. Whoever drinks it is one person again, for ever.

Un passo avanti. Nel bicchiere il colore.easy: A step forward. In the glass the colour reaches violet and stops there, stubbornly, as if waiting for something. One ingredient is still missing, and none of your books says which: the impurity that was in the first batch, which no one ever wrote down.
Un passo avanti. Nel bicchiere il colore.short: It reaches violet, and stops. The first batch's impurity is missing, and no one ever wrote it down.

Qualcuno, in famiglia, ricorda le parole.easy: Someone in the family remembers old Lomax's words at the General Store: *grey, it was grey*. The problem is not knowing its colour. It is knowing where to find it.
Qualcuno, in famiglia, ricorda le parole.short: *Grey, it was grey*, said Lomax. But where to find it?

Lo bevi in un sorso. Sa di niente, come.easy: You drink it in one gulp. It tastes of nothing, like water. For an hour nothing happens. Then you sit down, grow sleepy, and wake the next morning with a strange silence in your head, like when the rain stops. You look in the mirror. There is only one face.
Lo bevi in un sorso. Sa di niente, come.short: You drink it. You fall asleep, and wake with silence in your head. In the mirror there is one face.

Il topo beve, si lava i baffi e si addor.easy: The mouse drinks, washes its whiskers and falls asleep. The next morning it is alive, awake and perfectly normal. It is also, for the first time since it was caged, not interested in escaping at all. You are not sure that is good news.
Il topo beve, si lava i baffi e si addor.short: The mouse drinks and sleeps. Next morning it is normal, and no longer wants to escape. Good news?

Al manicomio, il figlio della donna in n.easy: At the asylum, the son of the woman in black drinks the glass without asking anything, laughing. By mid-afternoon he stops laughing. In the evening he asks for his mother, in his own voice, and she comes running, in her dressing gown, through the rain.
Al manicomio, il figlio della donna in n.short: The son of the woman in black drinks, and stops laughing. That evening he asks for his mother, in his own voice.

Nella chiesa nuova, tutta stucchi e oro,.easy: In the new church, all stucco and gold, a woman in black lights one candle after another before the altar, until the sexton tells her that is enough. Her son is one of the new-salt boys. Two years ago he drank it for a bet, and since then he has lived in the gentlefolk's ward, laughing.
Nella chiesa nuova, tutta stucchi e oro,.short: In church a woman in black lights candles. Her son drank the new salt for a bet, and has laughed in the asylum ever since.

Ti riconosce: tutta la città conosce la.easy: She recognises you: the whole town knows the family at the estate. She does not accuse you. She only asks, in the voice of someone who has already asked everyone, whether there is a way to bring him back.
Ti riconosce: tutta la città conosce la.short: She knows you, but does not accuse you. She only asks if there is a way to bring him back.

La donna ti prende la mano tra le sue e.easy: The woman takes your hand in hers and squeezes it hard, without a word. She leaves the church standing straighter than when she came in. You stay there, before the candles, wondering how many promises this family has made in fifty years, and how many it has kept.
La donna ti prende la mano tra le sue e.short: She squeezes your hand and leaves standing straighter. You wonder how many promises your family has kept.

La donna prende il denaro e ti ringrazia.easy: The woman takes the money and thanks you loudly, so that everyone hears. Soon the town is saying the family at the estate pays for the new-salt boys' care. Some see it as an admission of guilt. Most, for once, see a kindness.
La donna prende il denaro e ti ringrazia.short: She takes the money and thanks you aloud. The town says you pay for the salt boys' care: guilt to some, kindness to most.

Glielo dici piano, con le parole più sem.easy: You tell her gently, in the simplest words you can find. She nods, as if she already knew. Then she tells you about her son: he does not sleep, does not eat, writes letters with his left hand and signs them with a name that is not his. She tells you everything, for a whole hour, and you listen.
Glielo dici piano, con le parole più sem.short: You tell her the truth. She already knew. Then she talks of her son for an hour, and you listen.

Le redazioni dei due giornali sono una d.easy: The two papers' offices face each other across the same square, and their editors have not spoken in twenty years. As soon as they hear you are in the square, both send a boy to you with a visiting card. And both offer you the same thing: the front page, an exclusive interview about the family and Umber, and the facts told the way you prefer.
Le redazioni dei due giornali sono una d.short: Both papers offer you the front page: an interview about Umber, told the way you like.

Il giornale liberale scrive che Umber è.easy: The liberal paper writes that Umber is a bored rich man, perhaps a professor at the Institute, who enjoys frightening the poor. The conservative paper replies that the liberal paper is paid by the estate. For a week the town argues over the papers, and no one looks your way.
