Il giornale liberale scrive che Umber è.short: The liberal paper calls Umber a bored rich man. The other says it is paid by you. For a week no one looks your way.

Il giornale conservatore scrive che Umbe.easy: The conservative paper writes that Umber is a poor man dressed as a gentleman, one of the many who sleep in the lodging houses by the station. The next night the police raid the lodging houses. None of those arrested is Umber. For a while the estate has peace.
Il giornale conservatore scrive che Umbe.short: The conservative paper says Umber is poor. The police raid the lodging houses. For a while you have peace.

Racconti la storia vera due volte, a due.easy: You tell the true story twice, to two different reporters, and get paid twice. The next day, for the first time in their history, both papers come out with the same headline: *THE SALT OF THE ESTATE*. The town talks of nothing else. In the morning, on the estate door, someone has drawn in chalk a little man in a black coat.
Racconti la storia vera due volte, a due.short: You tell both the truth. They run the same headline: *THE SALT OF THE ESTATE*. On your door someone chalks a little man in black.

Al mercato c'è un banco nuovo, coperto d.easy: At the market there is a new stall covered in mirrors of every size: pocket mirrors, dressing-table mirrors, wall mirrors, in gilt frames and rough wooden ones. The seller has a white beard and a glass eye. "True mirrors," he says. "They show what is there." You pick one at random and look into it.
Al mercato c'è un banco nuovo, coperto d.short: At the market a man with a glass eye sells "true mirrors, that show what is there". You look into one.

Ti vedi vecchio, molto più vecchio di ad.easy: You see yourself old, much older than now, with the eyes of the portrait in the estate library. The seller nods, pleased. "You look like someone," he says. "Everyone looks like someone."
Ti vedi vecchio, molto più vecchio di ad.short: You see yourself old, with the eyes of the library portrait. "Everyone looks like someone," says the seller.

Nello specchio non c'è niente: il mercat.easy: There is nothing in the mirror: the market behind you, the people, the stall, but not you. The seller gives you back your coin without a word and turns his back on you.
Nello specchio non c'è niente: il mercat.short: The mirror shows everything but you. The seller returns your coin and turns away.

Dietro di te, nello specchio, c'è un pic.easy: Behind you, in the mirror, is a little man in a black coat, waving at you. You turn round: no one. When you look in the mirror again, the man is farther away, and waves again, the way you wave to someone leaving.
Dietro di te, nello specchio, c'è un pic.short: In the mirror, behind you, a little man in black waves. You turn: no one. He is farther now, and waves again.

Dietro di te, nello specchio, c'è il not.easy: Behind you, in the mirror, stands Ezra Pell the notary, hat in hand, smiling. You turn to greet him: no one. The seller looks at the mirror, then at you, then at the mirror again, and covers the stall with a cloth. "That's enough for today," he says.
Dietro di te, nello specchio, c'è il not.short: In the mirror, behind you, Ezra Pell smiles. You turn: no one. The seller covers his stall: "That's enough for today."

Il notaio Ezra Pell ha donato alla Libra.easy: Ezra Pell the notary has given the Library his father's archive: forty years of deeds, wills and letters, in a hundred cardboard boxes, carefully catalogued. The librarian is very proud of it. Only one box is missing, number 61, for the year 1861. The notary, she says, kept it, "for family reasons".
Il notaio Ezra Pell ha donato alla Libra.short: Ezra Pell gave the Library his father's archive. Only box 61, for 1861, is missing: he kept it.

Le lettere del vecchio a Silas sono brev.easy: The old man's letters to Silas are short, fond, full of formulas and jokes. The last ones, from 1860, are different: shorter, more nervous, in handwriting that is starting to slant. The very last says only: *Forgive me for the cupboard. I could not ask you: you would have said no.* Silas never replied. Or the reply is in box 61.
Le lettere del vecchio a Silas sono brev.short: The old man's last letter to Silas, from 1860, says: *Forgive me for the cupboard. I could not ask you: you would have said no.* The reply, if any, is in box 61.

La bibliotecaria scrive. Il notaio rispo.easy: The librarian writes. The notary replies by return of post, in handwriting so shaky that she has to read it with a magnifying glass: box 61 was destroyed in a small fire in his office, many years ago. The librarian says she is sorry. You wonder why a fire would pick a single box.
La bibliotecaria scrive. Il notaio rispo.short: The notary replies, in a shaking hand, that box 61 burned years ago. Just one box?

Le sei boccette del bisnonno sono ancora.easy: Your great-grandfather's six phials are still in the zinc box, under the loose board by the stove: broken sealing wax, faded labels, *Lomax's Pharmacy – first batch*. On the glass at the bottom is the same greyish film as ever. No one in the family has ever had the courage to scrape it off.
Le sei boccette del bisnonno sono ancora.short: Your great-grandfather's six phials are still under the board. The grey film still clings to the bottom.

Con un ago e molta pazienza raccogli, da.easy: With a needle and great patience you gather from all six a pinch of grey powder, so little it fits on the tip of a knife. In the glass, with the new salt, the colour reaches violet, hesitates, and for an instant turns green.
Con un ago e molta pazienza raccogli, da.short: You scrape out a pinch of grey powder. With the new salt the colour reaches violet, and for a moment turns green.

Il rettore dell'Istituto le compra senza.easy: The Institute's rector buys them without haggling, and puts them in a display case in the main corridor, with a handwritten card: *The original phials.* The students walk past them every day. At night, someone leaves a violet there.
Il rettore dell'Istituto le compra senza.short: You sell them to the Institute, which displays them. At night someone leaves a violet there.

Al catasto, nel municipio, l'impiegato t.easy: At the land registry, in the town hall, the clerk shows you with embarrassment a deed of purchase just filed. Someone has bought the strip of land along the alley behind the estate, and paid with a cheque. The cheque is genuine: it is signed by one of your grandparents, in 1877, in their upright hand. But the amount and the payee's name were written last week, in the backward-slanting hand.
Al catasto, nel municipio, l'impiegato t.short: Someone bought the alley with a cheque one of your grandparents signed in 1877. The amount and name, though, are from last week, slanting backwards.

Paghi, e il vicolo, da oggi, è di propri.easy: You pay, and from today the alley belongs to a certain Mr. Umber, with a proper notarial deed. It was drawn up, you notice, by the Pell office. And the notary charged no fee.
Paghi, e il vicolo, da oggi, è di propri.short: You pay. The alley now belongs to Mr. Umber, by a deed from the Pell office. Free of charge.

Il giudice ti dà ragione, dopo un mese d.easy: After a month of hearings the judge finds in your favour. The signature is genuine, but the cheque is void: the signer has been dead for thirty years. But the town followed the whole trial, and now it knows that in 1877 an heir of the estate signed a blank cheque to Mr. Umber.
Il giudice ti dà ragione, dopo un mese d.short: You win the case. But now the whole town knows that in 1877 one of your grandparents signed Umber a blank cheque.

Il fabbro è un vecchio con le braccia an.easy: The blacksmith is an old man with arms still strong and a tongue still loose: forty years ago he was the apprentice, the one with the toothless key. He remembers the little gentleman in the black coat perfectly. "He paid with cheques," he says. "Always good."
Il fabbro è un vecchio con le braccia an.short: The blacksmith was the apprentice of the toothless key. He remembers the little gentleman in black: "Paid by cheque. Always good."

Poi ti guarda meglio. \"Voi siete della.easy: Then he looks at you more closely. "You're from the estate. I made a copy of that key for your family, years ago. And another one last year."
Poi ti guarda meglio. \"Voi siete della.short: "You're from the estate. I made you a copy years ago. And another last year."

Poi abbassa la voce. \"Lo stampo l'ho te.easy: Then he lowers his voice. "I kept the mould, you know. And last year it came in handy."
Poi abbassa la voce. \"Lo stampo l'ho te.short: "I kept the mould. And last year it came in handy."

Il fabbro intasca le monete e si gratta.easy: The blacksmith pockets the coins and scratches his beard. "An elderly gentleman, distinguished, with gloves," he says. "Never took his gloves off. This time he paid cash, and wanted a receipt. The receipt had an office stamp on it."
Il fabbro intasca le monete e si gratta.short: "An elderly gentleman in gloves he never took off. Paid cash. The receipt had an office stamp."

Il fabbro te lo vende con un po' di rimp.easy: The blacksmith sells it to you somewhat reluctantly, wrapped in an oily cloth. It is a block of plaster with the print of a toothless key with an eye-shaped head. At home you put it on the mantelpiece. The next morning it is cracked, as if someone had squeezed it too hard.
Il fabbro te lo vende con un po' di rimp.short: You buy the key's mould. The next morning it is cracked, as if someone had squeezed it too hard.

Per i cinquant'anni dalla posa della pri.easy: For the asylum's fiftieth anniversary, the town council has decided to honour "the benefactors of the town's science". At the Foundry a bronze statue of the old man of the estate is being cast: tall, distinguished, with the Journal under his arm, as in the portrait. The foreman proudly shows you the mould. He says the committee paid with a very generous anonymous donation.
Per i cinquant'anni dalla posa della pri.short: The Foundry is casting a statue of the old man, tall and distinguished as in the portrait. An anonymous donor paid for it.

Il nome della famiglia viene inciso sul.easy: The family's name is carved on the pedestal, under the old man's, in smaller letters. At the unveiling the mayor makes a speech about progress, and the band plays. The statue looks sternly over the square. At night someone puts a black hat on its head.
Il nome della famiglia viene inciso sul.short: Your name goes on the pedestal. The band plays at the unveiling. At night someone puts a black hat on the statue.

Il caposquadra ti guarda come un pazzo,.easy: The foreman looks at you as if you were mad, but for a tip he redoes the head. The new face is that of an ordinary man, ageless and expressionless. The committee does not notice, nor does the town. Only Pell the notary, at the unveiling, stops before the statue and says quietly: "That's a better likeness."
Il caposquadra ti guarda come un pazzo,.short: The statue now has an ordinary face. No one notices but Pell the notary: "That's a better likeness."

Di notte entri nella fonderia e versi un.easy: At night you get into the foundry and pour a bucket of water into the still-hot mould. The bronze cracks with the sound of a broken bell. At dawn the statue has a crack across its face, from forehead to chin, and the town talks of nothing else. The police open a file.
Di notte entri nella fonderia e versi un.short: At night you pour water into the hot mould. The statue's face cracks. The police open a file.

Il funerale di Lomax è povero e breve: i.easy: Lomax's funeral is poor and short: the priest, two bored great-nephews, an old woman who sold soap beside his counter, and no customers. Ezra Pell the notary is in the front row, in black gloves. During the blessing he takes off one glove and lays a little bunch of violets on the coffin.
Il funerale di Lomax è povero e breve: i.short: At Lomax's poor funeral, Ezra Pell wears black gloves. He removes one and lays violets on the coffin.

Lo scalpellino incide il nome di Lomax,.easy: The stonemason carves Lomax's name, the dates and a line of your choosing: *He sold salt. It was pure.* The great-nephews cannot make sense of it. The notary, when he reads it, takes off his hat.
Lo scalpellino incide il nome di Lomax,.short: You have carved: *He sold salt. It was pure.* The notary takes off his hat.

Ezra ti saluta con un cenno e ti tiene a.easy: Ezra greets you with a nod and keeps you beside him for the whole service, the way one keeps a relative close. At the end he squeezes your arm. "He was a good man," he says. "He carried a secret for more than fifty years. I know how heavy it is."
Ezra ti saluta con un cenno e ti tiene a.short: Ezra keeps you close like a relative. "He carried a secret for fifty years. I know how heavy it is."

Resti in fondo, vicino alla porta. Da lì.easy: You stay at the back, by the door. From there you see what cannot be seen from the front row: when the notary takes off his glove, his right hand has violet-stained fingers, and it trembles. When he puts the glove back on, it stops trembling.
Resti in fondo, vicino alla porta. Da lì.short: From the back you see the notary's ungloved hand: violet-stained fingers, trembling.

La compagnia che da più di vent'anni rec.easy: The company that has performed *The Doctor and His Double* for more than twenty years gives its last show, then breaks up: the manager is old, the actors are tired, and the town has the cinematograph. The tent is full. In the front row are the mayor, the Institute's rector and Ezra Pell the notary, in his gloves.
La compagnia che da più di vent'anni rec.short: Last show of *The Doctor and His Double*. In the front row, among others, Ezra Pell, in gloves.

L'attore che fa Umber porta il cappotto.easy: The actor playing Umber wears the black coat you gave him. They say tonight he is better than ever.
L'attore che fa Umber porta il cappotto.short: The actor playing Umber wears your coat. Tonight he is superb.

Nel terzo atto il dottore insegue il dop.easy: In the third act the doctor chases the double across the rooftops, catches him and pulls off his hat. Tonight, under the hat, is not his son's face: it is an old, thin, tired face. The manager swears afterwards that the actor was never made up like that. Pell the notary, in the front row, leaves before the applause.
Nel terzo atto il dottore insegue il dop.short: Tonight, under the double's hat, is an old, tired face no one made up. Pell the notary leaves before the applause.

Dietro le quinte, tra i costumi appesi,.easy: Backstage, among the hanging costumes, you find the actor who plays Umber sitting on a trunk, head in his hands. "I don't know any more when I stop acting," he tells you. "Twenty years inside this character. Some nights I leave the tent and walk about, and people run, and I like it." He asks you for money for the train. He wants to leave tonight.
Dietro le quinte, tra i costumi appesi,.short: The actor who plays Umber is in despair: "I don't know when I stop acting. People run, and I like it." He wants money to leave tonight.

La lapide senza nome del vecchio, quella.easy: The old man's nameless headstone, the one the family had scraped clean years ago, has been cleaned. Someone has carved the name again, in small, careful letters, and underneath, even smaller: *Not yet.*
La lapide senza nome del vecchio, quella.short: Someone has recarved the old man's name on the headstone. And beneath it: *Not yet.*

Sotto il nome del vecchio e le parole *T.easy: Under the old man's name and the words *Come back soon*, which the family had carved years ago, someone has added with a nail, in a backward-slanting hand: *Almost.*
Sotto il nome del vecchio e le parole *T.short: Under *Come back soon*, someone has scratched with a nail, slanting backwards: *Almost.*

Sulla tomba del vecchio, la lapide è al.easy: On the old man's grave the headstone is in place, with the name and the two dates. But the earth in front has been freshly turned, as if someone had dug and filled it in again at night, carefully.
Sulla tomba del vecchio, la lapide è al.short: The old man's headstone is in place. But the earth is freshly turned, as if dug at night.

Sulla pietra c'è un mazzetto di violette.easy: On the stone is a little bunch of fresh violets, tied with string.

Il custode borbotta, ma per un'ora di la.easy: The keeper grumbles, but for an hour's work and a few coins he opens it again. The coffin is still there, empty. But at the bottom there is something that was not there fifty years ago: a notary's leather case, empty too, with the initials scraped off.
Il custode borbotta, ma per un'ora di la.short: You have the grave opened. In the empty coffin now lies a notary's case, its initials scraped off.

Le porti via, e il giorno dopo ci sono d.easy: You take them away, and the next day they are back. The keeper swears he has never seen who brings them. Then, after a tip, he admits he has sometimes seen, at dawn, an elderly gentleman with gloves. "A respectable sort," he says. "Don't you worry."
Le porti via, e il giorno dopo ci sono d.short: You remove them, and they return. For a tip the keeper admits: at dawn an elderly gentleman in gloves comes.

Il Memorial Institute è tutto vetro e ot.easy: The Memorial Institute is all glass and brass. The corridors smell of carbolic acid, and the professors in white coats walk fast, as if someone were chasing them. The rector receives you in an office full of microscopes. In front of him is a newspaper cutting about the estate's salt, underlined in red.
Il Memorial Institute è tutto vetro e ot.short: The Memorial Institute's rector receives you among microscopes, with an article on the salt underlined in red.

Vuole la formula. Vuole gli appunti dell.easy: He wants the formula. He wants the family's notes, the Journal, everything. In return he offers a sum that makes your head spin, and a chair named after the old man.
Vuole la formula. Vuole gli appunti dell.short: He wants the formula and the Journal. He offers a fortune and a chair in the old man's name.

Il rettore firma l'assegno senza discute.easy: The rector signs the cheque without arguing. A week later, in the Institute's windows, there is a poster: *The estate's salt: science in the service of the people*. It does not say which people.
Il rettore firma l'assegno senza discute.short: You sell. The Institute announces *The estate's salt: science in the service of the people*. It does not say which.

Il rettore ci pensa a lungo, poi ti pres.easy: The rector thinks it over for a long time, then introduces you to two young, sharp assistants with yellow-stained fingers. They work with you for three nights. They do not find the impurity, but they teach you a method for looking for it.
Il rettore ci pensa a lungo, poi ti pres.short: Two assistants work with you for three nights. They do not find the impurity, but teach you how to look.

Rifiuti con gentilezza, e il rettore ti.easy: You politely refuse, and the rector shows you out just as politely. In the corridor, through a half-open door, you see a professor pouring white salt into a glass of water, and waiting. The colour turns red, and stops there.
Rifiuti con gentilezza, e il rettore ti.short: You refuse. In the corridor a professor tests the salt: the colour turns red, and stops.

Il parente accusato per Umber, tanti ann.easy: The relative accused of being Umber, years ago, is still in a cell, because no one has ever dared reopen the case. They have grown old within those walls: thin, bent, with the pale eyes of someone who has looked out of a window for twenty years. The window looks onto the alley.
Il parente accusato per Umber, tanti ann.short: The relative accused years ago is still in a cell, old and bent. The window looks onto the alley.

\"Lo vedo passare, sai\", ti dice. \"Qua.easy: "I see him go by, you know," they tell you. "Nearly every night. Umber. He's not what he was: he's grown old too."
\"Lo vedo passare, sai\", ti dice. \"Qua.short: "I see him go by nearly every night. He has grown old too."

\"Cammina con un bastone nuovo, d'ebano\.easy: "He walks with a new ebony stick," they say. "And he carries a leather bag, the kind with a brass clasp, like doctors. Or notaries. Sometimes he stops under my window and raises his hat. He knows me. I think he's sorry."
\"Cammina con un bastone nuovo, d'ebano\.short: "He has an ebony stick and a leather bag, like a doctor's. Or a notary's. Sometimes he raises his hat. I think he's sorry."

Il secondino conta il denaro, si gratta.easy: The warder counts the money, scratches his head and one night "forgets" to lock the cell door. The relative comes back to the estate at dawn, on foot, their shoes dirty with mud from the alley. All spring they plant roses in the garden, and never speak of what they saw from the window.
Il secondino conta il denaro, si gratta.short: You pay the warder, and one night the cell is left open. The relative comes home and plants roses. They never speak of what they saw.

Il conto del vostro bisnonno è ancora ap.easy: Your great-grandfather's account is still open, after fifty years. The Bank's manager has changed three times, but the ledger is the same, kept under lock and key like a relic. The last withdrawal was yesterday. The signature slants backwards, and shakes.
Il conto del vostro bisnonno è ancora ap.short: Your great-grandfather's account has been open fifty years. The last withdrawal was yesterday, with a shaky, backward-slanting signature.

I versamenti, dice il direttore, li port.easy: The manager says the deposits are still brought by the clerk from the Pell's notary practice. He is an old man now, and no longer smiles.
I versamenti, dice il direttore, li port.short: The deposits still come with Pell's clerk, now old.

Il direttore te lo mostra sotto la lampa.easy: The manager shows it to you under the lamp. The handwriting is the usual one, small, backwards. The ink is not: it is violet, that sharp violet you cannot buy in stationers' shops and that only notaries' offices use, for deeds that cannot be forged.
Il direttore te lo mostra sotto la lampa.short: The handwriting is the usual. The ink is violet: the kind only notaries' offices use.

Il tribunale ci mette un mese, e alla fi.easy: The court takes a month, and in the end finds for the family: the account is frozen until the final reading of the will. The day after the ruling, on the estate doorstep, there is a cheque torn into eight pieces.
Il tribunale ci mette un mese, e alla fi.short: The court freezes the account. The next day, on your doorstep, lies a cheque torn into eight pieces.

Seppelliscono l'Ispettore Nell Haskett i.easy: Inspector Nell Haskett is buried on a sunny day, at eighty-six, with the police band and two speeches that go on too long. Ada is in the front row, in her old inspector's coat, holding her aunt's black notebook tight. Ezra Pell the notary is at the cemetery too, at the back, by the gate. He leaves before the blessing.
Seppelliscono l'Ispettore Nell Haskett i.short: Nell Haskett is buried at eighty-six. Ada clutches her aunt's black notebook. Ezra Pell, at the back, leaves before the blessing.

Ada esita, poi te lo porge. \"La zia dic.easy: Ada hesitates, then hands it to you. "My aunt said you could be trusted," she says. "One of you, at least." The pages hold fifty years of notes in block capitals. The last entry on Umber is from 1895: *The cheques change. Same hand, but heavier. It begins the winter young Pell stops sleeping.*
Ada esita, poi te lo porge. \"La zia dic.short: Ada hands you the notebook. The last entry on Umber, from 1895: *The cheques change. Same hand, but heavier. It begins the winter young Pell stops sleeping.*

Ada stringe il taccuino al petto. \"La z.easy: Ada holds the notebook to her chest. "My aunt left it to me," she says. "And you never trusted her. Why should I trust you?" She turns away, back to her aunt.
Ada stringe il taccuino al petto. \"La z.short: "You never trusted her. Why should I trust you?" Ada keeps the notebook.

Lasci un fiore sulla tomba e ti fermi un.easy: You leave a flower on the grave and stand there a moment. Nearby, on Silas Pell's headstone, is a little bunch of fresh violets, tied with string. The keeper says the notary brings them every morning, at dawn.
Lasci un fiore sulla tomba e ti fermi un.short: On Silas Pell's headstone are fresh violets. The keeper says the notary brings them every morning at dawn.

All'ufficio del catasto, nel municipio,.easy: At the land registry, in the town hall, you meet Ezra Pell the notary. He has come to file a deed, and is waiting his turn on a bench, hat on his knees. He is very thin, he coughs, and he wears gloves even indoors.
All'ufficio del catasto, nel municipio,.short: At the land registry you meet Ezra Pell: very thin, coughing, gloved even indoors.

Sotto il braccio ha un libro che riconos.easy: Under his arm is a book you recognise: the *Essay on the Dual Nature of Man*, with the library card sticking out of its pages.
Sotto il braccio ha un libro che riconos.short: Under his arm is the *Essay on the Dual Nature of Man*.

Ti chiede, con un interesse che non ries.easy: He asks you how your antidote is coming along, with an interest he cannot hide.
Ti chiede, con un interesse che non ries.short: He asks, too keenly, about the antidote.

Ezra ascolta, annuisce, fa due domande p.easy: Ezra listens, nods, asks two precise questions about temperature and timing. Then he opens his wallet and gives you money "for laboratory expenses, in memory of my father". When you thank him, he looks at you the way one looks at someone about to leave.
Ezra ascolta, annuisce, fa due domande p.short: Ezra listens, asks two precise questions and gives you money for the laboratory. He looks at you like someone about to leave.

Ezra si toglie un guanto, lentamente. Ha.easy: Ezra slowly takes off a glove. His fingers are stained with violet ink. He takes the pen in his right hand and starts to write, in an upright, tidy, notary's hand. Halfway through his name the hand stiffens, and the last letters bend backwards. Ezra looks at the sheet, crumples it, puts it in his pocket and leaves without waiting his turn.
Ezra si toglie un guanto, lentamente. Ha.short: Ezra removes a glove: violet fingers. He writes his name upright, but the last letters bend backwards. He crumples the sheet and leaves.

Lo saluti e te ne vai. Sulla soglia ti v.easy: You say goodbye and leave. In the doorway you turn round: Ezra Pell is still on the bench, staring into space, his gloved hands clutching his hat. In the glass of the door his reflection is smaller than he is.
Lo saluti e te ne vai. Sulla soglia ti v.short: You leave. In the door's glass, Ezra's reflection is smaller than he is.

Gli eredi di Lomax svendono tutto quello.easy: Lomax's heirs are selling off everything from the old pharmacy: boxes, jars, little scales, yellowed prescriptions, whole drawers of unlabelled powders. It is all heaped on a table at the back of the General Store, and people rummage through it as at a flea market.
Gli eredi di Lomax svendono tutto quello.short: Lomax's heirs sell off the old pharmacy: jars, prescriptions, drawers of unlabelled powders.

In fondo al cassetto, dentro una bustina.easy: At the bottom of the drawer, in a carefully folded paper packet, is a pinch of grey powder. It tastes of nothing. In the laboratory, dissolved with the new salt, it takes the colour from violet to green, for an instant, before it turns back. There is little of it. But it is the one.
In fondo al cassetto, dentro una bustina.short: At the bottom of the drawer is a pinch of grey powder. With the new salt the colour reaches green, for a moment. There is little, but it is the one.

Nel cassetto ci sono polveri di ogni col.easy: In the drawer there are powders of every colour: white, yellow, pink, even a blue one. No grey ones. You take them home anyway. Some of them, at least, are useful.
Nel cassetto ci sono polveri di ogni col.short: Powders of every colour, but no grey. You take them anyway.

Sono dodici volumi rilegati in tela, umi.easy: There are twelve cloth-bound volumes, damp from the cellar. In the fourth, under the date 9 November 1859, is the crossed-out line you know, or have heard of. With a magnifying glass and a candle behind the page, the ink under the crossing-out can still be read: *grey powder, from S. P.'s cupboard.*
Sono dodici volumi rilegati in tela, umi.short: In the 1859 ledger, under the crossed-out line, you can still read: *grey powder, from S. P.'s cupboard.*

Il sale di quella prima partita era mio,.easy: The salt of that first batch was mine, but it was not pure. One winter evening the old man from the estate came to the pharmacy with a phial of grey powder. He asked me to mix it into the salt, a teaspoon per phial, and not to write it in the ledger. He paid me not to write it: enough to buy the pharmacy twice over, and my silence for more than fifty years.
Il sale di quella prima partita era mio,.short: The first batch was not pure. The old man had me mix in a grey powder, a teaspoon per phial, and paid me to keep quiet for fifty years.

Gli chiesi da dove venisse quella polver.easy: I asked him where the powder came from. He said he had taken it from a friend's cupboard, a man of law who had trained as an apothecary when young and kept his powders under lock and key. And that the friend must not know. The notary. Your father, Mr. Pell. The good salt was never the old man's discovery: it was a theft.
Gli chiesi da dove venisse quella polver.short: The powder came from the notary's cupboard, your father's, Mr. Pell, without his knowing. The good salt was not a discovery: it was a theft.

Una boccetta di quella partita l'ho tenu.easy: I kept one phial of that batch myself. Just one, for fifty years, at the bottom of a drawer. I never opened it. Take it, and do what you like with it: I want nothing more to do with it.
Una boccetta di quella partita l'ho tenu.short: I kept one phial of that batch, never opened. Take it.

Ho trascritto queste parole con la mano.easy: I wrote these words with a steady hand. It was the last time.
Ho trascritto queste parole con la mano.short: I wrote this with a steady hand. For the last time.

Lomax muore la notte stessa, con le mani.easy: Lomax dies that same night, hands folded. The phial passes to {0}, who wraps it in a handkerchief and puts it in their inside jacket pocket, over the heart. It weighs more than it should.
Lomax muore la notte stessa, con le mani.short: Lomax dies that night. The phial passes to {0}, who keeps it over the heart. It weighs more than it should.

Nessuno la vuole. Lomax muore la notte s.easy: No one wants it. Lomax dies that same night, the phial clutched in his hand. When the nurse tries to take it from him, his fingers will not open. They bury him like that. The next day, on his grave, someone has left a flower and a cheque.
Nessuno la vuole. Lomax muore la notte s.short: No one wants it. Lomax dies holding the phial, and is buried with it. On his grave, a flower and a cheque.

Il giornale liberale e quello conservato.easy: For once the liberal paper and the conservative one come out with the same front-page news: Lomax the chemist, the salt man, is dead. Naturally the two versions differ. For the liberal paper he was a small shopkeeper crushed by the powerful. For the conservative one, a poisoner saved by old age.
Il giornale liberale e quello conservato.short: Lomax is dead. For one paper he was a victim of the powerful, for the other a poisoner saved by old age.

Tutti e due ricordano, nell'articolo, la.easy: In the article both recall the "surprising interview" given months ago by an heir of the estate, who told the story of the salt to both papers and got paid twice. Both call it "illuminating".
Tutti e due ricordano, nell'articolo, la.short: Both recall your interview, paid twice. They call it "illuminating".

Il giornale liberale ricorda di aver sem.easy: The liberal paper recalls that it always said Umber was a bored rich man. The conservative paper recalls that it always said the liberal paper was paid by the estate.
Il giornale liberale ricorda di aver sem.short: Each paper recalls that it was always right.

Il giornale conservatore ricorda con org.easy: The conservative paper proudly recalls the raids on the station lodging houses, which "restored order". The liberal paper recalls that none of those arrested was Umber.
Il giornale conservatore ricorda con org.short: One recalls the raids proudly. The other recalls that none of those arrested was Umber.

In seconda pagina, una lettera al dirett.easy: On page two is a letter to the editor from a mother whose son is in the gentlefolk's ward. She thanks "a family in town" that has promised her a cure. The letter is signed only with initials.
In seconda pagina, una lettera al dirett.short: A mother thanks "a family in town" that promised her son a cure.

La Library annuncia con soddisfazione di.easy: The Library is pleased to announce that it has catalogued the archive of the late Silas Pell, notary, donated by his son. The catalogue is open to the public. The year 1861, it notes, is missing.
La Library annuncia con soddisfazione di.short: The Library has catalogued Silas Pell's archive. The year 1861 is missing.

Nella cronaca, un trafiletto: il vecchio.easy: In the local news, a short item: the town's old blacksmith has shut up shop and gone to live with his daughter. He says that lately too many people were asking him about a key "very old and very strange".
Nella cronaca, un trafiletto: il vecchio.short: The old blacksmith has shut up shop: too many asked about a key "very old and very strange".

L'Istituto di scienze sulla collina ha c.easy: The Institute of Science on the hill has changed its mind: now it offers a fortune for the salt's formula, and a chair to whoever brings it. The professors come to the estate by motor car, wearing gloves.
L'Istituto di scienze sulla collina ha c.short: The Institute now offers a fortune for the salt's formula. The professors arrive by motor car.

Cari amici, perché ormai posso chiamarvi.easy: Dear friends, for I may call you that now: I am writing because I need to tell someone, and my aunt is gone.
Cari amici, perché ormai posso chiamarvi.short: Dear friends, I write because I must tell someone, and my aunt is gone.

Signori, non siamo mai stati amici, e no.easy: Ladies and gentlemen, we have never been friends, and I shall not pretend to be now. I am writing because I have no one else to write to, and because what I have to say concerns you more than anyone.
Signori, non siamo mai stati amici, e no.short: We have never been friends. But what I have to say concerns you more than anyone.

Sono cinquantadue anni che la mia famigl.easy: For fifty-two years my family has hunted Mr. Umber. My aunt started when she was younger than I am now. I carried on when she could no longer manage. We stopped forty short men and a few innocents, and closed more than one file out of weariness. We never caught him.
Sono cinquantadue anni che la mia famigl.short: For fifty-two years my family has hunted Umber. We stopped many innocents. Never him.

Avete visto la statua del vecchio, in pi.easy: Have you seen the old man's statue in the square? Everyone says it looks like him. I never saw the old man. But walking past it at night, I had the feeling the statue looked like someone else.
Avete visto la statua del vecchio, in pi.short: Everyone says the statue looks like the old man. At night, to me it looks like someone else.

Il taccuino della zia, che vi ho lasciat.easy: My aunt's notebook, which I let you read at the cemetery, I have read again myself, all of it, at night. I read the last page on Umber three times. I think in the end she had understood, and did not have the courage to write it all down.
Il taccuino della zia, che vi ho lasciat.short: I reread my aunt's notebook. I think in the end she understood, but lacked the courage to write it.

So che uno di voi è andato alla Bank a v.easy: I know one of you went to the Bank to see the last cheque from the old account. Violet ink, wasn't it? I saw it too. There are few places in this town where that ink is used.
So che uno di voi è andato alla Bank a v.short: I know about the last cheque. Violet ink, wasn't it? Few places in town use it.

So anche che siete andati a trovare il v.easy: I also know you visited your relative in the cell, and that they told you about the old gentleman with the leather bag. They never told me. Perhaps I never asked the right way.
So anche che siete andati a trovare il v.short: I know about the old gentleman with the leather bag too. Your relative never told me.

Non ho più il distintivo, e non ho più l.easy: I no longer have the badge, nor the age for it. But if one day you need someone who knows how to listen, you know where I live. Ada Haskett.
Non ho più il distintivo, e non ho più l.short: If you need someone to listen, you know where I live. Ada Haskett.

I giornali, per una volta d'accordo, ann.easy: For once the papers agree: the worst storm in fifty years is coming. That afternoon a note arrives at the estate from Ezra Pell the notary, in a hand so shaky it is hard to read. He wants to see the whole family on the night of the storm, in the room with two doors. He will bring the will.
I giornali, per una volta d'accordo, ann.short: The worst storm in fifty years is coming. Pell the notary writes: that night he will bring the will, to the room with two doors.

Rispondete con un biglietto di due righe.easy: You reply with a two-line note: the family will expect him. The office clerk collects it at the door and leaves without waiting for a tip.
Rispondete con un biglietto di due righe.short: You reply that you will expect him.

Ada Haskett, ormai in pensione, accetta.easy: Ada Haskett, retired now, accepts at once. "My aunt said she never liked that notary," she says. "She couldn't say why. I'll be there."
Ada Haskett, ormai in pensione, accetta.short: Ada Haskett accepts at once: "My aunt never liked that notary. I'll be there."

Ada Haskett vi fa rispondere dalla sua g.easy: Ada Haskett has her housekeeper reply: she is retired, and your family has never been kind to hers. On the night of the storm she will stay at home.
Ada Haskett vi fa rispondere dalla sua g.short: Ada Haskett refuses: your family was never kind to hers.

Passate dallo studio Pell nel pomeriggio.easy: In the afternoon you call at the Pell office, on some pretext. The notary is out, and the clerk has you wait in the files room. In a corner stands an old walnut cupboard, its doors open. There is nothing inside, only a bitter smell and a grey film on the shelves.
Passate dallo studio Pell nel pomeriggio.short: At the Pell office you see the old cupboard, open. It is empty: only a bitter smell and a grey film.

Il cielo sopra la città è basso e giallo.easy: The sky over the town is low and yellow. In every house the shutters are closing. Tonight the notary will read the will for the last time.
Il cielo sopra la città è basso e giallo.short: The sky is yellow. Tonight the will is read for the last time.

Prima che arrivi il notaio ti chiudi in.easy: Before the notary arrives you lock yourself in the bathroom with Lomax's phial and a glass of water. You break the seal. The salt is white, fine as sugar, with a yellowish sheen when you hold it to the light. A sentence you have never read comes back to you, who knows from where: *a single sip. Then the door.*
Prima che arrivi il notaio ti chiudi in.short: Before the notary arrives you lock yourself in with Lomax's phial. A sentence you never read comes back to you: *a single sip. Then the door.*

Nessuno saprà che cosa hai scelto, finch.easy: No one will know what you chose until it is too late to change it.
Nessuno saprà che cosa hai scelto, finch.short: No one will know what you chose until it is too late.

Il temporale arriva al tramonto. La fami.easy: The storm breaks at sunset. The family is gathered in the room with two doors, among the old man's mirrors, and the electric light flickers on and off. Ezra Pell the notary stands by the fireplace, in a wet coat, the will in his hand. He has grown old all at once, like someone who has not slept for years.
Il temporale arriva al tramonto. La fami.short: At sunset, in the study of mirrors, Ezra Pell waits with the will in his hand. He looks as if he has not slept for years.

\"Le circostanze sono dubbie da cinquant.easy: "The circumstances have been doubtful for fifty years," he says. "The will obliges me to hand everything to Mr. Umber. Before I do, I want you to tell me what I must do." Outside, thunder rattles the windows, and for a moment, in every mirror, the notary looks smaller.
\"Le circostanze sono dubbie da cinquant.short: "The will obliges me to give everything to Mr. Umber. Tell me what I must do." For a moment, in the mirrors, the notary looks smaller.

Il cappotto nero è appeso all'attaccapan.easy: The black coat hangs on the hall coat stand, where you put it. Coming in, the notary hangs his hat on it without thinking, as one does at home.
Il cappotto nero è appeso all'attaccapan.short: Coming in, the notary hangs his hat on the black coat, as if at home.

In un angolo, seduta, c'è Ada Haskett, i.easy: In a corner sits Ada Haskett: retired, but with her aunt's notebook on her knees. The notary greets her with a bow, and from then on never turns his back on her.
In un angolo, seduta, c'è Ada Haskett, i.short: In the corner sits Ada Haskett, with her aunt's notebook. The notary never turns his back on her.

Nessuno di voi lo dice ad alta voce. Ma.easy: None of you says it aloud. But while the notary speaks, you all watch his hands, and the gloves he never takes off. Over these years each of you has seen something: a signature, an ink, a name on a card, an open door. On their own, they mean nothing. Put together, they make a single person. And in the mirrors, for a moment, you all see the same thing.
Nessuno di voi lo dice ad alta voce. Ma.short: While the notary speaks, you all watch his gloves. Each of you has seen something. Together, those things make one person. And in the mirrors you all see the same thing.

Qualcuno di voi, chissà perché, non ries.easy: One of you, who knows why, cannot stop looking at the notary's hands.
Qualcuno di voi, chissà perché, non ries.short: One of you cannot stop looking at the notary's hands.

Sul tavolo c'è l'antidoto, un bicchiere.easy: On the table is the antidote, one glass each. The notary looks at it as one looks at a weapon.
Sul tavolo c'è l'antidoto, un bicchiere.short: On the table is the antidote. The notary eyes it like a weapon.

I cronisti dei due giornali aspettano fu.easy: The reporters from both papers wait outside the gate, in the rain. You would only have to open the door and tell everything.
I cronisti dei due giornali aspettano fu.short: Outside, in the rain, the reporters wait.

Il notaio apre il testamento sul tavolo,.easy: The notary opens the will on the table, at the page with the clause. His hand shakes so much that he has to steady it with the other.
Il notaio apre il testamento sul tavolo,.short: The notary opens the will at the clause. His hand shakes.

Ada Haskett visse altri vent'anni, nella.easy: Ada Haskett lived another twenty years, in her aunt's little house near the station, with the cat and the black notebook. Every Christmas she received a box of apples and a note from the estate, and every Christmas she replied with two lines: *Nothing yet. I'm keeping an eye on you.*
Ada Haskett visse altri vent'anni, nella.short: Ada Haskett lived another twenty years. Every Christmas she answered your apples: *Nothing yet. I'm keeping an eye on you.*

Ada Haskett lasciò la città l'anno dopo,.easy: Ada Haskett left town the following year without saying goodbye to anyone, and went to live in a seaside town where no one had ever heard of Umber. They say she was happy there. They also say that at night she checked the lock twice.
Ada Haskett lasciò la città l'anno dopo,.short: Ada Haskett moved to the sea, where no one knew Umber. They say she was happy, and checked the lock twice.

Lo studio sul vicolo, quello degli specc.easy: The room on the alley, the study of mirrors, which **{0}** had found years before by following the footprints in the mud, stayed as it was. The door with no handle never opened again from the alley. From inside, sometimes, it did.
Lo studio sul vicolo, quello degli specc.short: The study of mirrors, found by **{0}**, stayed as it was. From the alley the door never opened again. From inside, sometimes, it did.

Nell'archivio del manicomio sulla collin.easy: In the archive of the asylum on the hill there is still the file of the gentlefolk's ward's first important patient, an heir of the estate, with the diagnosis written by Lady Carew herself: *interesting case*.
Nell'archivio del manicomio sulla collin.short: The asylum still keeps the committed heir's file: *interesting case*.

La cella della Jail con la finestra sul.easy: The Jail cell with the window on the alley, where an innocent member of the family spent so many years, has been closed and turned into a records room. At night the constables do not like going in. They say you can see someone go by from the window.
La cella della Jail con la finestra sul.short: The cell on the alley is a records room now. The constables say that at night someone can be seen passing the window.

Il processo all'Erede nell'Ombra, l'unic.easy: The trial of the Heir in the Shadow, the only time the town managed to lay hands on Umber, is still studied in law schools, as the case of a culprit who did not remember his crime. The professors agree on nothing. The students enjoy it enormously.
Il processo all'Erede nell'Ombra, l'unic.short: The Heir in the Shadow's trial is still studied in law schools. The professors argue, the students enjoy it.

Sulla tomba del vecchio, sotto il nome,.easy: On the old man's grave, under the name, you can still read the words the family had carved: *Come back soon*. Every few years someone goes over them with a chisel, so the moss does not cover them.
Sulla tomba del vecchio, sotto il nome,.short: On the old man's grave *Come back soon* can still be read: someone recuts it every few years.

La tomba del vecchio, senza nome, è la p.easy: The old man's nameless grave is the most visited in the cemetery. People bring children there, to frighten them. They bring flowers, for luck. And every morning the violets are always there.
La tomba del vecchio, senza nome, è la p.short: The old man's nameless grave is the most visited. Every morning the violets are there.

Il notaio Ezra Pell è sepolto nel cimite.easy: Ezra Pell the notary is buried in the new cemetery, by the wall, under a lime tree, in a grave paid for twenty-five years earlier with a cheque. The headstone says only: *Here lies the one who kept the key*.
Il notaio Ezra Pell è sepolto nel cimite.short: Ezra Pell lies under the lime tree, in the grave Umber paid for: *Here lies the one who kept the key*.

La statua di bronzo del vecchio è ancora.easy: The old man's bronze statue is still in the square, the Journal under its arm. The pigeons prefer it to all the others. In the evening lovers meet beneath it. And no one can explain why, at a certain hour, the statue's shadow is much shorter than the statue.
La statua di bronzo del vecchio è ancora.short: The old man's statue still stands in the square. At a certain hour its shadow is much shorter than it is.

Il cappotto nero del vecchio è finito, d.easy: When the company broke up, the old man's black coat ended up in a junk dealer's storeroom. Every so often someone buys it. And every time, after a few weeks, the dealer finds it hanging on his door again, carefully folded.
Il cappotto nero del vecchio è finito, d.short: The black coat is at a junk dealer's. Whoever buys it, within weeks it is back on his door.

Il fascicolo Pell, o quello che ne resta.easy: The Pell file, or what is left of it, is what you have just finished reading. If you read it in order, skipping nothing, you already know who closed it. If you think you recognise the handwriting of the last pages, do not stop to think about it. Close it and go to bed. With the light on, perhaps.
Il fascicolo Pell, o quello che ne resta.short: This is the Pell file. If you recognise the handwriting of the last pages, don't think about it. Go to bed. With the light on.

La città aveva già preso Umber una volta.easy: The town had caught Umber once before, and had liked it. When the sightings began again, no one wanted to wait for another expert's report. One night in March they came to the estate with torches, and left with one of us: the one who wrote fastest, and whose hand, when writing fast, slanted backwards. The trial lasted an afternoon. They put up the gallows in the square, in front of the Jail, where the market used to be.
La città aveva già preso Umber una volta.short: When Umber returned, the town did not wait. They came with torches and took one of us, the one whose hand slanted backwards. The trial lasted an afternoon. They put the gallows up in the square.

Non era lui. Lo so perché la notte dopo.easy: It was not him. I know because the night after the hanging, at the far end of the cemetery, by the gate, someone laughed for a whole hour. Everyone heard it, and no one went out to look.
Non era lui. Lo so perché la notte dopo.short: It was not him. The next night, in the cemetery, someone laughed for an hour.

Il notaio Ezra Pell assistette all'esecu.easy: Ezra Pell the notary watched the execution from the front row, hat in hand, and died a month later. When we opened his file, the last pages were written in a small, quick hand that slanted backwards. The last line said only: *I am sorry. It was not him. It was me.*
Il notaio Ezra Pell assistette all'esecu.short: Ezra Pell died a month later. The last line of his file, slanting backwards: *I am sorry. It was not him. It was me.*

La forca l'hanno smontata il giorno dopo.easy: They took the gallows down the next day, and the wood was sold at auction. The travelling players' theatre bought it for next to nothing and built a new stage with it. Since then, whenever I go to the theatre, I sit in the back row, near the door.
La forca l'hanno smontata il giorno dopo.short: The gallows wood became the theatre's stage. Since then I sit near the door.

Ada Haskett, che quella notte era con no.easy: Ada Haskett, who was with us in the room that night, refused to testify at the trial. She returned her aunt's black notebook to the police, with a two-line letter, and left town.
Ada Haskett, che quella notte era con no.short: Ada Haskett refused to testify. She returned her aunt's notebook and left town.

I due giornali hanno pubblicato la nostr.easy: On the day of the hanging both papers printed our whole story, under the same headline as a year before. This time there was a photograph beneath it.
I due giornali hanno pubblicato la nostr.short: The papers printed our story under the same headline as before. This time with a photograph.

Scrivo con l'altra mano, perché questa è.easy: I write with the other hand, because it is mine now. The heir who used it before me drank the new salt one evening, to see if they could go back. They could not. They had been halfway across since birth, and the new salt only shut the door.
Scrivo con l'altra mano, perché questa è.short: I write with the other hand: it is mine now. The heir before me drank the new salt to go back. It only shut the door.

Non lo rimpiango. Era una persona noiosa.easy: I do not regret it. They were a dull person: slept at night, paid their debts, apologised. I do not. I broke every mirror in the room, so that neither of us would need to look at the other again, and I have been very well ever since.
Non lo rimpiango. Era una persona noiosa.short: I do not regret it: they were dull. I broke every mirror, and I have been very well since.

Una cosa sola, prima di chiudere questo.easy: One thing only, before I close this notebook, so the family cannot say Umber does not pay his debts. I did not sign all the cheques of the last twenty years. On the night of the storm, in the room, there was another of us: standing by the fireplace, in a wet coat, the will in his hand. I saw him in the mirrors, before I broke them. He was laughing with my own mouth.
Una cosa sola, prima di chiudere questo.short: One more thing: I did not sign all the last twenty years' cheques. On the night of the storm, by the fireplace, stood another of us, the will in his hand. He laughed with my mouth.

Chiedete al notaio che cosa c'era nella.easy: Ask the notary what was in his father's cupboard. Ask him soon: he has not got long.
Chiedete al notaio che cosa c'era nella.short: Ask the notary what was in the cupboard. Soon.

La famiglia mi tratta con gentilezza, co.easy: The family treats me kindly, the way one treats a sick relative. At night they leave me the laboratory and the door onto the alley. In the morning they find the glasses washed and the Journal up to date, in a backward-slanting hand that is, I must say, far easier to read than yours.
La famiglia mi tratta con gentilezza, co.short: The family treats me like a sick relative. At night I use the laboratory. My handwriting is easier to read than yours.

Avete bruciato il mio cappotto. Non impo.easy: You burned my coat. It does not matter: I bought another just like it, with your money.
Avete bruciato il mio cappotto. Non impo.short: You burned my coat. I bought another, with your money.

Il sale nuovo di Lomax non si è più ferm.easy: Lomax's new salt never stopped. Students buy it for a bet, ladies out of boredom, bankers for courage. Lomax sold more than he could make, and after his death the Institute of Science bought the recipe, and sells it with a smarter label and a higher price.
Il sale nuovo di Lomax non si è più ferm.short: Everyone buys the new salt. After Lomax died, the Institute bought the recipe and sells it dear.

La nostra famiglia, in tutto questo, non.easy: Our family no longer counts for anything in all this. We are the old man's relatives, the ones who started it, and people greet us in the street with absent-minded respect, the way one greets an inventor's descendants. In the evening some of us go out with the others. No one asks who.
La nostra famiglia, in tutto questo, non.short: Our family no longer counts: we are just the relatives of those who started it. At night some of us go out with the others. No one asks who.

Sull'etichetta c'è il nome del vecchio,.easy: The label bears the old man's name, in gold letters. The Institute has made good use of the notes we sold it.
Sull'etichetta c'è il nome del vecchio,.short: The label bears the old man's name, in gold: the Institute made good use of our notes.

Chi lo beve non torna indietro, ma nessu.easy: Those who drink it do not go back, but no one seems to mind. By day {0} is a town like any other, hard-working and respectable. By night half its people leave home with another face, smaller, quicker, and meet in the alleys to laugh. The police have stopped counting the cheques. The papers have stopped writing about Umber: there are too many of them.
Chi lo beve non torna indietro, ma nessu.short: By day {0} is respectable. By night half its people go out with another face, laughing in the alleys. There are too many Umbers.

Il notaio Ezra Pell è morto in autunno,.easy: Ezra Pell the notary died in the autumn, in his bed. In his will he left everything to the Institute, "so that science may finish what my family began". The signature is genuine: three experts checked it. It slants backwards.
Il notaio Ezra Pell è morto in autunno,.short: Ezra Pell died and left everything to the Institute. The signature is genuine. It slants backwards.

Vi scrivo con la mano di {0}, perché è l.easy: I am writing to you with {0}'s hand, because it is the only one I have. Lomax's salt was the last of it, and it was good. When {1} drank it, on the night of the storm, the door opened from the other side, and I came back in. Not as Umber: as myself. The old man of the estate, the one you buried under seventy kilograms of stones.
Vi scrivo con la mano di {0}, perché è l.short: I write with {0}'s hand. When {1} drank Lomax's salt, the door opened, and I came back in: the old man of the estate.

{0} c'è ancora, da qualche parte. Lo sen.easy: {0} is still in here somewhere. I feel it in the morning, when I tie my shoes; then it passes. Do not worry: I shall look after the estate better than you did. I have fifty years of work to make up, and at last a young body to do it with.
{0} c'è ancora, da qualche parte. Lo sen.short: {0} is still in here somewhere. I have fifty years of work to make up, and at last a young body.

Prima di cominciare, una questione d'ono.easy: Before I begin, a matter of honour. Yesterday Ezra Pell the notary came to see me, my friend's son. Years ago he found the powder in his father's cupboard, and used it as I had: it was he who signed the cheques, when none of you was me. He is tired, and asked me if there is a way back. I told him the truth: there is none. Then I offered him a glass.
Prima di cominciare, una questione d'ono.short: Ezra Pell, my friend's son, used his father's powder as I did: he signed the cheques. He asked me the way back. There is none. I offered him a glass.

Sono passato dalla piazza, stamattina, a.easy: This morning I walked through the square, on {0}'s legs, which are good legs. The town has changed. The wooden houses are gone, the river is covered, the market has become a prison. The cemetery, though, is just the same. I stopped in front of my grave. I left some violets.
Sono passato dalla piazza, stamattina, a.short: This morning, on {0}'s legs, I went to my grave. I left some violets.

Avevate fatto incidere sulla mia lapide.easy: On my headstone you had carved: *Come back soon*. I took you at your word. It took me fifty years, but I kept my word too.
Avevate fatto incidere sulla mia lapide.short: You wrote *Come back soon*. It took me fifty years, but I kept my word.

Ringrazio anche chi, in famiglia, ha por.easy: I also thank those in the family who brought the notary what he asked for, without asking questions. A page, a pinch of salt, a key, a hair: without you he would not have found his way here. Nor would I.
Ringrazio anche chi, in famiglia, ha por.short: Thanks to those who brought the notary what he asked. Without you, we would not have found the way.

Bevemmo l'antidoto la notte del temporal.easy: We drank the antidote on the night of the storm, all together, in the room with two doors. Nothing spectacular happened: a little nausea, great sleepiness, and in the morning a strange silence in the head, like when the rain stops. Since that night no one has seen Umber.
Bevemmo l'antidoto la notte del temporal.short: We drank the antidote together, on the night of the storm. No one has seen Umber since.

Con lui se n'è andato anche il resto. Le.easy: With him went everything else. Our formulas no longer work, the experiments fail, the Journal seems to be written in a language we can no longer read. We have become what the town always wanted: a respectable family, with a house too big and nothing to say. We are terribly bored.
Con lui se n'è andato anche il resto. Le.short: With him went everything: formulas, experiments, the Journal. Now we are respectable. We are terribly bored.

La porta sul vicolo l'abbiamo murata la.easy: The week after, we bricked up the door onto the alley, with new bricks and white mortar. For a month, every morning, we found scratches on the plaster on the alley side, at the height of a small man. Then nothing more. The bricklayer says it was cats.
La porta sul vicolo l'abbiamo murata la.short: We bricked up the alley door. For a month we found scratches outside, at a small man's height. Then nothing.

Una cosa buona, però, l'abbiamo fatta. I.easy: One good thing, though, we did. The son of the woman in black, the first we gave the antidote to, has been home for months. On Sundays he is in church, in the front row, with his mother. When he sees us, he raises his hat.
Una cosa buona, però, l'abbiamo fatta. I.short: One good thing we did: the son of the woman in black is cured. When he sees us, he raises his hat.

Una cosa buona, però, l'abbiamo fatta. I.easy: One good thing, though, we did. The day after the storm we took a glass of antidote to the asylum, to the son of the woman in black. By mid-afternoon he stopped laughing. In the evening he walked home with his mother, and the next Sunday they were both in church, in the front row.
Una cosa buona, però, l'abbiamo fatta. I.short: One good thing we did: we gave the antidote to the son of the woman in black. He stopped laughing and went home with his mother.

Il notaio Ezra Pell bevve il suo bicchie.easy: Ezra Pell the notary drank his glass last that night, after looking at it for a long time. He died in his sleep three days later, smiling. When we opened his file, the last pages were written in two hands, alternating line by line, one slanting forward and one backwards. Halfway down the last page the two hands became one, and the final sentence read: *At last, one.*
Il notaio Ezra Pell bevve il suo bicchie.short: Ezra Pell drank last, and died smiling three days later. In his file two hands alternated, then became one: *At last, one.*

Chi di noi aveva assaggiato l'antidoto p.easy: The one of us who tasted the antidote first, in the laboratory, says the silence in the head has never gone away. They say at first it was a blessing. Now, some evenings, they sit at the window and wait for someone who does not come.
Chi di noi aveva assaggiato l'antidoto p.short: The one who tasted the antidote first still has the silence in their head. Some evenings they wait at the window for someone who never comes.

Il sottoscritto, notaio in {0}, dà esecu.easy: The undersigned, notary in {0}, executes the clause in the late testator's will, first read by his father Silas Pell in March 1861. The circumstances of the testator's death having been found doubtful, all property not left to the heirs, the money in the bank, the shares and the key to the room on the alley pass to Mr. Umber.
Il sottoscritto, notaio in {0}, dà esecu.short: The undersigned, notary in {0}, executes the clause: the circumstances were doubtful, and the unassigned property, with the key to the room on the alley, passes to Mr. Umber.

Il beneficiario si è presentato nello st.easy: The beneficiary came to the undersigned's office in person and in broad daylight, as his father required fifty years ago, at twelve o'clock sharp. He signed the receipt in a small hand that slants backwards. The undersigned certifies his identity in full knowledge of the facts: he sees him every morning in the mirror.
Il beneficiario si è presentato nello st.short: The beneficiary came in person, at noon, and signed slanting backwards. The undersigned certifies his identity: he sees him every morning in the mirror.

La famiglia conserva la tenuta, il labor.easy: The family keeps the estate, the laboratory and the name. From now on Umber shall have only the key. The undersigned believes that, for a man who always used the back door, this is more than enough.
La famiglia conserva la tenuta, il labor.short: The family keeps the estate and the name. Umber gets only the key. It is enough for him.

La famiglia ha assistito alla consegna i.easy: The family watched the handover in silence, in the undersigned's office, seated in a row as at a funeral. The beneficiary shook each one's hand, called each one by name and asked after everyone's health. He knew every name, every illness, every debt. He said it was a pleasure, at last, to meet in person.
La famiglia ha assistito alla consegna i.short: The family watched in silence. Umber shook every hand, calling each by name. He knew every illness and every debt.

Il sottoscritto ringrazia gli eredi che,.easy: The undersigned thanks those heirs who in recent months secretly brought him what he asked for. Without their help this execution would not have been possible.
Il sottoscritto ringrazia gli eredi che,.short: The undersigned thanks those who secretly brought what he asked. Without them it would not have been possible.

Il beneficiario ritira inoltre le sei bo.easy: The beneficiary also takes back the six empty phials the family entrusted to the undersigned many years ago, kept in the office's glass cabinet. He takes them back washed.
Il beneficiario ritira inoltre le sei bo.short: Umber also takes back the six phials. Washed.

Aprimmo il cancello ai cronisti la matti.easy: The morning after the storm we opened the gate to the reporters, and told everything: the salt, the phials, the old man in the coffin of stones, the Heir in the Shadow, the broken stick. For once both papers agreed, and put our confession on the front page. For a month {0} talked of nothing else.
Aprimmo il cancello ai cronisti la matti.short: After the storm we told the reporters everything. Our confession made the front page, and {0} talked of nothing else.

Abbiamo perso il nome. Nessuno ci invita.easy: We have lost our good name. No one invites us to dinner any more, the bank has closed our accounts, and children cross the street when we pass. But no one has arrested us: no court knows how to try a man for what his other self does, and no judge wanted to be the first to try. We are free, and alone, and for the first time in fifty years we sleep at night.
Abbiamo perso il nome. Nessuno ci invita.short: We lost our name, the invitations and the accounts. But no judge knows how to try a man for his other self. We are free, alone, and sleep at last.

Abbiamo confessato tutto. Quasi tutto. Q.easy: We confessed everything. Almost everything. When Ezra Pell the notary died, in December, at the back of his file we found a page he had never shown anyone, in the backward-slanting hand: *They confessed all they knew. They did not know about me.*
Abbiamo confessato tutto. Quasi tutto. Q.short: We confessed almost everything. In Ezra Pell's file, after his death, a page slanting backwards: *They confessed all they knew. They did not know about me.*

I bambini della città, adesso, cantano u.easy: Now the town's children sing a new rhyme as they skip: *Umber, Umber, where is he? He was there, now let him be.* When we pass they do not stop singing. They look at us, smile, and now and then someone waves.
I bambini della città, adesso, cantano u.short: The children sing: *Umber, Umber, where is he? He was there, now let him be.* When we pass, they wave.

Il giornale liberale, che anni prima ave.easy: The liberal paper, which years before had written that Umber was a bored rich man, printed our confession under a headline that made us laugh: *We Told You So.*
Il giornale liberale, che anni prima ave.short: The liberal paper's headline: *We Told You So.*

Il giornale conservatore, che anni prima.easy: The conservative paper, which years before had sent the police into the poor men's lodging houses, put our confession on the back page, among the death notices. We deserved it.
Il giornale conservatore, che anni prima.short: The conservative paper put us among the death notices. We deserved it.

Il notaio Ezra Pell è deceduto il giorno.easy: Ezra Pell the notary died on the 2nd of this month, in his office, of natural causes. The doctor who confirmed the death saw the body.
Il notaio Ezra Pell è deceduto il giorno.short: Ezra Pell died on the 2nd. The doctor saw the body.

Il testamento del defunto non è stato es.easy: The deceased's will has not been executed, and the family at the estate has asked that the papers remain sealed. The family's file, sealed and marked *to be opened after my death*, was collected on the 3rd, before anyone opened it. It was collected by a gentleman short in stature, in a black coat too big for him, with a proper authorisation signed by the deceased. The signature has been checked and is genuine. It slants backwards.
Il testamento del defunto non è stato es.short: The family's sealed file was collected on the 3rd by a small gentleman in a black coat, with the deceased's authorisation. The signature is genuine. It slants backwards.

Il signore ha ringraziato, ha messo il f.easy: The gentleman said thank you, tucked the file under his arm and left by the service door, whistling. The undersigned, a clerk of the office, feels he must record this, because the office has no service door.
Il signore ha ringraziato, ha messo il f.short: He left by the service door, whistling. The office has no service door.

Il sottoscritto aggiunge, per completezz.easy: The undersigned adds, for completeness, that in the deceased's armchair, the one facing the empty cupboard, a man's black hat was found, of small size, which no one in the office remembers ever seeing. It was taken to the lost property office, where so far no one has come to claim it.
Il sottoscritto aggiunge, per completezz.short: In the deceased's armchair, facing the empty cupboard, lay a small black hat. No one has claimed it.

Si annota infine che, dieci minuti dopo,.easy: Finally, ten minutes later the heirs of the estate arrived at the office, with Ada Haskett, retired inspector, asking for the file and the deceased's personal papers. They were too late. Before leaving, one of them asked to see the signature on the authorisation, and looked at it for a long time without a word.
Si annota infine che, dieci minuti dopo,.short: Ten minutes later the heirs arrived, with Ada Haskett. Too late. One of them studied the signature for a long time, in silence.

Si annota inoltre che dall'armadio a vet.easy: It is also recorded that six empty phials of dark glass, belonging to the family at the estate, are missing from the office's glass cabinet. The clerk cannot say when they disappeared.
Si annota inoltre che dall'armadio a vet.short: The family's six phials are also missing from the glass cabinet.
